```
+type CompletionFollowUpStep =

+
+function defaultErrorCode(status: number): string {
+  if (status === 401) return 'authentication_failed';
+  if (status === 403) return 'forbidden';
+  if (status === 404) return 'not_found';
+  if (status === 405) return 'method_not_allowed';
+  if (status === 429) return 'rate_limited';
+  if (status === 503) return 'service_unavailable';
+  if (status >= 500) return 'internal_server_error';
+  return 'request_failed';
+}
+
+function completeTaskErrorResponse(
+  message: string,

+      message,
+      recoverable: status >= 500 || status === 429,

+    status,
+  );

+
+function asObjectRecord(value: unknown): Record<string, unknown> {
+  if (!value || typeof value !== 'object' || Array.isArray(value)) {
+    return {};
+  }
+  return value as Record<string, unknown>;
+}
+
+async function persistCompletionFollowUpIssues(

+    return { ok: true };

+
+  const baseResultData = asObjectRecord(existingResultData);
+  const completionFollowUp = {
+    status: 'degraded',
+    recorded_at: new Date().toISOString(),
+    issues,
+  };
+
+  const { error } = await supabase
+    .from('tasks')
+    .update({
+      result_data: {
+        ...baseResultData,
+        completion_follow_up: completionFollowUp,
+      },
+    })
+    .eq('id', taskId);
+
+  if (error) {
+    return { ok: false, error };
+  }
+
+  return { ok: true };
```

```
index 3d087353..e59f7a31 100644
--- a/supabase/functions/_shared/rateLimit.ts

@@ -288,3 +288,65 @@ export function rateLimitFailureResponse(
   }
   return rateLimitResponse(extractDeniedResultFromFailure(result, config), config);
 }
+
+interface RateLimitLogger {
+  warn: (message: string, context?: Record<string, unknown>) => void;
+  error: (message: string, context?: Record<string, unknown>) => void;
+  flush: () => Promise<void>;
+}
+
+/**
+ * Full rate-limit enforcement: check → error response → fail_open logging.
+ * Returns a Response to short-circuit (exceeded or service error), or null to proceed.
+ *
+ * @param serviceUnavailableResponse Optional factory for 503 responses.
+ *   Defaults to a generic 503 edge error.
+ */
+export async function enforceRateLimit(
+  supabaseAdmin: SupabaseAdminClient,
+  functionName: string,
+  userId: string,
+  config: RateLimitConfig,
+  logger: RateLimitLogger,
+  logPrefix: string,
+  serviceUnavailableResponse?: () => Response,
+): Promise<Response | null> {
+  const result = await checkRateLimit(supabaseAdmin, functionName, userId, config, logPrefix);
+
+  // Rate limit exceeded — works for both ok (fail_closed) and !ok paths
+  if (isRateLimitExceededFailure(result)) {
+    logger.warn('Rate limit exceeded', { user_id: userId });
+    await logger.flush();
+    if (result.ok) {
+      return rateLimitResponse(result.value, config);
+    }
+    return rateLimitFailureResponse(result, config);
+  }
+
+  // Operation failure that's not rate-limit-exceeded
+  if (!result.ok) {
+    logger.error('Rate limit check failed', {
+      user_id: userId,
+      error_code: result.errorCode,
+      message: result.message,
+    });
+    await logger.flush();
+    return serviceUnavailableResponse
+      ? serviceUnavailableResponse()
+      : edgeErrorResponse(
+          { errorCode: 'rate_limit_service_unavailable', message: 'Rate limit service unavailable', recoverable: true },
+          503,
+        );
+  }
+
+  // Success but degraded (fail_open) — proceed with warning
+  if (result.policy === 'fail_open') {
+    logger.warn('Rate limit check degraded; allowing request', {
+      user_id: userId,
+      reason: result.value.degraded?.reason,
+      message: result.value.degraded?.message,
+    });
+  }
+
+  return null;
+}
```

```
+import { getSupabaseClient } from '@/integrations/supabase/client';
+import type { Json } from '@/integrations/supabase/types';
+
+interface GenerationSettingsInput {
+  id: string;
+  projectId: string;
+}
+
+interface DeleteGenerationVariantInput {
+  id: string;
+  generationId: string;
+}
+
+interface CreateGenerationRecordInput {
+  imageUrl: string;
+  thumbnailUrl: string;
+  fileType: string;
+  projectId: string;
+  generationParams: Record<string, Json | undefined>;
+}
+
+interface CreatePrimaryVariantInput {
+  generationId: string;
+  imageUrl: string;
+  thumbnailUrl: string;
+  generationParams: Record<string, Json | undefined>;
+  variantType: string;
+}
+
+export function updateGenerationLocationByScope(
+  params: GenerationSettingsInput & { location: string; thumbnailUrl?: string },
+) {
+  return getSupabaseClient()
+    .from('generations')
+    .update({
+      location: params.location,
+      ...(params.thumbnailUrl ? { thumbnail_url: params.thumbnailUrl } : {}),
+    })
+    .eq('id', params.id)
+    .eq('project_id', params.projectId)
+    .select('id');
+}
+
+export function createGenerationRecord(params: CreateGenerationRecordInput) {
+  return getSupabaseClient()
+    .from('generations')
+    .insert({
+      location: params.imageUrl,
+      thumbnail_url: params.thumbnailUrl,
+      type: params.fileType,
+      project_id: params.projectId,
+      params: params.generationParams,
+    })
+    .select()
+    .single();
+}
+
+export function createGenerationPrimaryVariant(params: CreatePrimaryVariantInput) {
+  return getSupabaseClient()
+    .from('generation_variants')
+    .insert({
+      generation_id: params.generationId,
+      location: params.imageUrl,
+      thumbnail_url: params.thumbnailUrl,
+      is_primary: true,
+      variant_type: params.variantType,
+      name: 'Original',
+      params: params.generationParams,
+    });
+}
+
+export function updateGenerationStarByScope(
+  params: GenerationSettingsInput & { starred: boolean },
+) {
+  return getSupabaseClient()
+    .from('generations')
+    .update({ starred: params.starred })
+    .eq('id', params.id)
+    .eq('project_id', params.projectId)
+    .select('id, starred');
+}
+
+export function deleteGenerationByScope(params: GenerationSettingsInput) {
+  return getSupabaseClient()
+    .from('generations')
+    .delete()
+    .eq('id', params.id)
+    .eq('project_id', params.projectId)
+    .select('id');
+}
+
+export function deleteGenerationVariantByScope(params: DeleteGenerationVariantInput) {
+  return getSupabaseClient()
+    .from('generation_variants')
+    .delete()
+    .eq('id', params.id)
+    .eq('generation_id', params.generationId)
+    .select('id');
+}
```

```
+import { fireEvent, render, screen } from '@testing-library/react';
+import { describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';
+import type { ReactNode } from 'react';
+import { StrokeOverlayCanvas } from './StrokeOverlayCanvas';
+
+const mocks = vi.hoisted(() => ({
+  Stage: vi.fn(
+    ({
+      children,
+      onPointerDown,
+      onPointerMove,
+      onPointerUp,
+    }: {
+      children?: ReactNode;
+      onPointerDown?: (event: unknown) => void;
+      onPointerMove?: (event: unknown) => void;
+      onPointerUp?: (event: unknown) => void;
+    }) => (
+      <div
+        data-testid="stage"
+        onPointerDown={() => onPointerDown?.({ type: 'down' })}
+        onPointerMove={() => onPointerMove?.({ type: 'move' })}
+        onPointerUp={() => onPointerUp?.({ type: 'up' })}
+      >
+        {children}
+      </div>
+    ),
+  ),
+  Layer: vi.fn(({ children }: { children?: ReactNode }) => <div data-testid="layer">{children}</div>),
+  Line: vi.fn(() => <div data-testid="line" />),
+  Rect: vi.fn(() => <div data-testid="rect" />),
+}));
+
+vi.mock('react-konva', () => ({
+  Stage: (props: unknown) => mocks.Stage(props),
+  Layer: (props: unknown) => mocks.Layer(props),
+  Line: (props: unknown) => mocks.Line(props),
+  Rect: (props: unknown) => mocks.Rect(props),
+}));
+
+describe('StrokeOverlayCanvas', () => {
+  const baseProps = {
+    displayWidth: 320,
+    displayHeight: 180,
+    strokes: [] as never[],
+    currentStroke: [] as Array<{ x: number; y: number }>,
+    selectedShapeId: null as string | null,
+    annotationMode: null as 'rectangle' | null,
+    isEraseMode: false,
+    brushSize: 4,
+    scaleX: 2,
+    toStage: (x: number, y: number) => ({ x, y }),
+    onPointerDown: vi.fn(),
+    onPointerMove: vi.fn(),
+    onPointerUp: vi.fn(),
+  };
+
+  it('returns null when dimensions are zero', () => {
+    const { container } = render(
+      <StrokeOverlayCanvas
+        {...baseProps}
+        displayWidth={0}
+        displayHeight={0}
+      />,
+    );
+
+    expect(container.firstChild).toBeNull();
+    expect(mocks.Stage).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
+  });
+
+  it('wires stage pointer handlers and renders persisted + current strokes', () => {
+    render(
+      <StrokeOverlayCanvas
+        {...baseProps}
+        strokes={[
+          {
+            id: 'rect-1',
+            shapeType: 'rectangle',
+            points: [{ x: 10, y: 20 }, { x: 30, y: 60 }],
+            isFreeForm: false,
+            isErasing: false,
+            brushSize: 3,
+          },
+          {
+            id: 'line-1',
+            shapeType: 'free',
+            points: [{ x: 0, y: 0 }, { x: 10, y: 10 }],
+            isFreeForm: false,
+            isErasing: true,
+            brushSize: 5,
+          },
+        ] as never}
+        currentStroke={[
+          { x: 5, y: 5 },
+          { x: 25, y: 25 },
+        ]}
+        annotationMode="rectangle"
+      />,
+    );
+
+    const stage = screen.getByTestId('stage');
+    fireEvent.pointerDown(stage);
+    fireEvent.pointerMove(stage);
+    fireEvent.pointerUp(stage);
+
+    expect(baseProps.onPointerDown).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
+    expect(baseProps.onPointerMove).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
+    expect(baseProps.onPointerUp).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
+

diff --git a/src/shared/components/MediaLightbox/components/strokeOverlay/StrokeOverlayCanvas.tsx b/src/shared/components/MediaLightbox/components/strokeOverlay/StrokeOverlayCanvas.tsx
new file mode 100644
index 00000000..b3c6d86a
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/shared/components/MediaLightbox/components/strokeOverlay/StrokeOverlayCanvas.tsx
@@ -0,0 +1,182 @@
+import { Stage, Layer, Line, Rect } from 'react-konva';
+import type { KonvaEventObject } from 'konva/lib/Node';
+import type { BrushStroke } from '../../hooks/inpainting/types';
+
+interface StrokeOverlayCanvasProps {
+  displayWidth: number;
+  displayHeight: number;
+  strokes: BrushStroke[];
+  currentStroke: Array<{ x: number; y: number }>;
+  selectedShapeId: string | null;
+  annotationMode: 'rectangle' | null;
+  isEraseMode: boolean;
+  brushSize: number;
+  scaleX: number;
+  toStage: (ix: number, iy: number) => { x: number; y: number };
+  onPointerDown: (e: KonvaEventObject<PointerEvent>) => void;
+  onPointerMove: (e: KonvaEventObject<PointerEvent>) => void;
+  onPointerUp: (e: KonvaEventObject<PointerEvent>) => void;
+}
+
+function renderStroke({
+  stroke,
+  selectedShapeId,
+  toStage,
+  scaleX,
+}: {
+  stroke: BrushStroke;
+  selectedShapeId: string | null;
+  toStage: (ix: number, iy: number) => { x: number; y: number };
+  scaleX: number;
+}) {
+  const isSelected = stroke.id === selectedShapeId;
+  const color = isSelected
+    ? 'rgba(0, 255, 100, 0.9)'
+    : stroke.isErasing
+      ? 'rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.5)'
+      : 'rgba(255, 0, 0, 0.7)';
+
+  if (stroke.shapeType === 'rectangle' && stroke.points.length >= 2) {
+    if (stroke.isFreeForm && stroke.points.length === 4) {
+      return (
+        <Line
+          key={stroke.id}
+          points={stroke.points.flatMap((point) => {
+            const stagePoint = toStage(point.x, point.y);
+            return [stagePoint.x, stagePoint.y];
+          })}
+          stroke={color}
+          strokeWidth={3}
+          closed
+        />
+      );
+    }
+
+    const start = toStage(stroke.points[0].x, stroke.points[0].y);
+    const end = toStage(stroke.points[1].x, stroke.points[1].y);
+    return (
+      <Rect
+        key={stroke.id}
+        x={Math.min(start.x, end.x)}
+        y={Math.min(start.y, end.y)}
+        width={Math.abs(end.x - start.x)}
+        height={Math.abs(end.y - start.y)}
+        stroke={color}
+        strokeWidth={3}
+      />
+    );
+  }
+
+  return (
+    <Line
+      key={stroke.id}
+      points={stroke.points.flatMap((point) => {
+        const stagePoint = toStage(point.x, point.y);
+        return [stagePoint.x, stagePoint.y];
+      })}
+      stroke={stroke.isErasing ? 'rgba(0, 0, 0, 1)' : color}
+      strokeWidth={stroke.brushSize * scaleX}
+      lineCap="round"
+      lineJoin="round"
+      globalCompositeOperation={stroke.isErasing ? 'destination-out' : 'source-over'}
+    />
+  );
+}
+
+function renderCurrentStroke({
+  currentStroke,
+  annotationMode,
+  toStage,
+  isEraseMode,
+  brushSize,
+  scaleX,
+}: {
+  currentStroke: Array<{ x: number; y: number }>;
+  annotationMode: 'rectangle' | null;
+  toStage: (ix: number, iy: number) => { x: number; y: number };
+  isEraseMode: boolean;
+  brushSize: number;
+  scaleX: number;
+}) {
+  if (currentStroke.length === 0) {
+    return null;
+  }
+
+  if (annotationMode === 'rectangle') {
+    const start = toStage(currentStroke[0].x, currentStroke[0].y);
+    const end = toStage(currentStroke[currentStroke.length - 1].x, currentStroke[currentStroke.length - 1].y);
+    return (
+      <Rect
+        x={Math.min(start.x, end.x)}
+        y={Math.min(start.y, end.y)}
+        width={Math.abs(end.x - start.x)}
+        height={Math.abs(end.y - start.y)}
+        stroke="rgba(100, 200, 255, 0.8)"
+        strokeWidth={3}
+        dash={[5, 5]}
+      />
+    );
+  }
+
+  return (
+    <Line
+      points={currentStroke.flatMap((point) => {
+        const stagePoint = toStage(point.x, point.y);
+        return [stagePoint.x, stagePoint.y];
+      })}
+      stroke={isEraseMode ? 'rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.5)' : 'rgba(255, 0, 0, 0.4)'}
+      strokeWidth={brushSize * scaleX}
+      lineCap="round"
+      lineJoin="round"
+    />
+  );
+}
+
+export function StrokeOverlayCanvas({
+  displayWidth,
+  displayHeight,
+  strokes,
+  currentStroke,
+  selectedShapeId,
+  annotationMode,
+  isEraseMode,
+  brushSize,
+  scaleX,
+  toStage,
+  onPointerDown,
+  onPointerMove,
+  onPointerUp,
+}: StrokeOverlayCanvasProps) {
+  if (displayWidth === 0 || displayHeight === 0) {
+    return null;
+  }
+
+  return (
+    <Stage
+      width={displayWidth}
+      height={displayHeight}
+      style={{ display: 'block', cursor: 'crosshair', touchAction: 'none' }}
+      onPointerDown={onPointerDown}
+      onPointerMove={onPointerMove}
+      onPointerUp={onPointerUp}
+      onPointerCancel={onPointerUp}
+    >
+      <Layer>
+        {strokes.map((stroke) => renderStroke({
+          stroke,
+          selectedShapeId,
+          toStage,
+          scaleX,
+        }))}
+        {renderCurrentStroke({
+          currentStroke,
+          annotationMode,
+          toStage,
+          isEraseMode,
+          brushSize,
+          scaleX,
+        })}
+      </Layer>
+    </Stage>
+  );
+}

+import { describe, it, expect, vi, beforeEach } from 'vitest';
+import { exportStrokeMask } from '../maskExport';
+import type { BrushStroke } from '../../../hooks/inpainting/types';
+
+// Konva needs a DOM container — jsdom provides this, but Konva.Stage.toDataURL
+// may not produce real pixel data. We test the function's structural behavior:
+// null for empty, non-null data URL for strokes, error resilience.
+
+function makeLineStroke(overrides?: Partial<BrushStroke>): BrushStroke {
+  return {
+    id: 'stroke-1',
+    points: [{ x: 10, y: 10 }, { x: 100, y: 100 }],
+    isErasing: false,
+    brushSize: 20,
+    shapeType: 'line',
+    ...overrides,
+  };
+}
+
+function makeRectStroke(overrides?: Partial<BrushStroke>): BrushStroke {
+  return {
+    id: 'rect-1',
+    points: [{ x: 10, y: 10 }, { x: 200, y: 200 }],
+    isErasing: false,
+    brushSize: 20,
+    shapeType: 'rectangle',
+    ...overrides,
+  };
+}
+
+function makeFreeFormRectStroke(): BrushStroke {
+  return {
+    id: 'freeform-1',
+    points: [
+      { x: 10, y: 10 },
+      { x: 200, y: 10 },
+      { x: 200, y: 200 },
+      { x: 10, y: 200 },
+    ],
+    isErasing: false,
+    brushSize: 20,
+    shapeType: 'rectangle',
+    isFreeForm: true,
+  };
+}
+
+describe('exportStrokeMask', () => {
+  beforeEach(() => {
+    vi.restoreAllMocks();
+  });
+
+  it('returns null when there are no strokes to export', () => {
+    const result = exportStrokeMask({
+      strokes: [],
+      imageWidth: 512,
+      imageHeight: 512,
+    });
+
+    expect(result).toBeNull();
+  });
+
+  it('returns a data URL for a line stroke', () => {
+    const result = exportStrokeMask({
+      strokes: [makeLineStroke()],
+      imageWidth: 256,
+      imageHeight: 256,
+    });
+
+    expect(result).not.toBeNull();
+    expect(result).toMatch(/^data:image\/png/);
+  });
+
+  it('returns a data URL for a rectangle stroke', () => {
+    const result = exportStrokeMask({
+      strokes: [makeRectStroke()],
+      imageWidth: 256,
+      imageHeight: 256,
+    });
+
+    expect(result).not.toBeNull();
+    expect(result).toMatch(/^data:image\/png/);
+  });
+
+  it('returns a data URL for a free-form rectangle stroke', () => {
+    const result = exportStrokeMask({
+      strokes: [makeFreeFormRectStroke()],
+      imageWidth: 256,
+      imageHeight: 256,
+    });
+
+    expect(result).not.toBeNull();
+    expect(result).toMatch(/^data:image\/png/);
+  });
+
+  it('handles multiple strokes of mixed types', () => {
+    const result = exportStrokeMask({
+      strokes: [makeLineStroke(), makeRectStroke(), makeFreeFormRectStroke()],
+      imageWidth: 512,
+      imageHeight: 512,
+    });
+
+    expect(result).not.toBeNull();
+    expect(result).toMatch(/^data:image\/png/);
+  });
+
+  it('skips strokes with fewer than 2 points', () => {
+    const result = exportStrokeMask({
+      strokes: [
+        makeLineStroke({ id: 'empty', points: [{ x: 0, y: 0 }] }),
+      ],
+      imageWidth: 256,
+      imageHeight: 256,
+    });
+
+    // The only stroke is skipped, but the mask is still generated (black background only)
+    expect(result).not.toBeNull();
+    expect(result).toMatch(/^data:image\/png/);
+  });
+
+  it('cleans up the offscreen container even when Konva throws', () => {
+    const originalCreateElement = document.createElement.bind(document);
+    const appendSpy = vi.spyOn(document.body, 'appendChild');
+    const removeSpy = vi.spyOn(document.body, 'removeChild');
+
+    // Sabotage the container so Konva.Stage fails
+    vi.spyOn(document, 'createElement').mockImplementation((tag: string) => {
+      const el = originalCreateElement(tag);
+      if (tag === 'div') {
+        Object.defineProperty(el, 'clientWidth', { get: () => { throw new Error('boom'); } });
+      }
+      return el;
+    });
+
+    const result = exportStrokeMask({
+      strokes: [makeLineStroke()],
+      imageWidth: 256,
+      imageHeight: 256,
+    });
+
+    // Should return null on error
+    expect(result).toBeNull();
+    // Container should still be cleaned up (finally block)
+    expect(removeSpy.mock.calls.length).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(appendSpy.mock.calls.length);
+  });
+
+  it('accepts a custom pixelRatio', () => {
+    // Just verify it doesn't throw with non-default pixelRatio
+    const result = exportStrokeMask({
+      strokes: [makeLineStroke()],
+      imageWidth: 128,
+      imageHeight: 128,
+      pixelRatio: 2,
+    });
+
+    expect(result).not.toBeNull();
+    expect(result).toMatch(/^data:image\/png/);
+  });
+});
diff --git a/src/shared/components/MediaLightbox/components/strokeOverlay/maskExport.ts b/src/shared/components/MediaLightbox/components/strokeOverlay/maskExport.ts
new file mode 100644
index 00000000..c23e5bd5
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/shared/components/MediaLightbox/components/strokeOverlay/maskExport.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,107 @@
+import Konva from 'konva';
+import { normalizeAndPresentError } from '@/shared/lib/errorHandling/runtimeError';
+import type { BrushStroke } from '../../hooks/inpainting/types';
+
+interface ExportStrokeMaskInput {
+  strokes: BrushStroke[];
+  imageWidth: number;
+  imageHeight: number;
+  pixelRatio?: number;
+}
+
+const DEFAULT_EXPORT_PIXEL_RATIO = 1.5;
+const MASK_BACKGROUND = 'black';
+const MASK_STROKE = 'white';
+const RECTANGLE_MASK_STROKE_WIDTH = 6;
+
+function addStrokeToMaskLayer(layer: Konva.Layer, stroke: BrushStroke): void {
+  if (stroke.points.length < 2) {
+    return;
+  }
+
+  if (stroke.shapeType === 'rectangle') {
+    if (stroke.isFreeForm && stroke.points.length === 4) {
+      layer.add(new Konva.Line({
+        points: stroke.points.flatMap(point => [point.x, point.y]),
+        stroke: MASK_STROKE,
+        strokeWidth: RECTANGLE_MASK_STROKE_WIDTH,
+        closed: true,
+        lineCap: 'round',
+        lineJoin: 'round',
+      }));
+      return;
+    }
+
+    const start = stroke.points[0];
+    const end = stroke.points[1];
+    layer.add(new Konva.Rect({
+      x: Math.min(start.x, end.x),
+      y: Math.min(start.y, end.y),
+      width: Math.abs(end.x - start.x),
+      height: Math.abs(end.y - start.y),
+      stroke: MASK_STROKE,
+      strokeWidth: RECTANGLE_MASK_STROKE_WIDTH,
+    }));
+    return;
+  }
+
+  layer.add(new Konva.Line({
+    points: stroke.points.flatMap(point => [point.x, point.y]),
+    stroke: MASK_STROKE,
+    strokeWidth: stroke.brushSize,
+    lineCap: 'round',
+    lineJoin: 'round',
+  }));
+}
+
+export function exportStrokeMask({
+  strokes,
+  imageWidth,
+  imageHeight,
+  pixelRatio = DEFAULT_EXPORT_PIXEL_RATIO,
+}: ExportStrokeMaskInput): string | null {
+  if (strokes.length === 0) {
+    return null;
+  }
+
+  const container = document.createElement('div');
+  container.style.position = 'absolute';
+  container.style.left = '-9999px';
+  document.body.appendChild(container);
+
+  try {
+    const stage = new Konva.Stage({
+      container,
+      width: imageWidth,
+      height: imageHeight,
+    });
+    const layer = new Konva.Layer();
+    stage.add(layer);
+
+    layer.add(new Konva.Rect({
+      x: 0,
+      y: 0,
+      width: imageWidth,
+      height: imageHeight,
+      fill: MASK_BACKGROUND,
+    }));
+
+    strokes.forEach((stroke) => addStrokeToMaskLayer(layer, stroke));
+
+    layer.draw();
+    const dataUrl = stage.toDataURL({
+      pixelRatio,
+      mimeType: 'image/png',
+    });
+    stage.destroy();
+    return dataUrl;
+  } catch (error) {
+    normalizeAndPresentError(error, {
+      context: 'StrokeOverlay.exportMask',
+      showToast: false,
+    });
+    return null;
+  } finally {
+    document.body.removeChild(container);
+  }
+}
```

```
+/**
+ * Resolve based_on generation ID from params.
+ * Extracts the based_on ID, verifies it exists in the DB, and falls back
+ * to image-URL lookup if the explicit ID is missing or stale.
+ */
+export async function resolveBasedOn(
+  supabase: SupabaseClient,
+  params: unknown,
+): Promise<string | null> {
+  const record = params && typeof params === 'object' && !Array.isArray(params)
+    ? params as Record<string, unknown>
+    : {};
+
+  let basedOnGenerationId: string | null = extractBasedOn(record);
+
+  if (basedOnGenerationId) {
+    const { data: basedOnGen, error: basedOnError } = await supabase
+      .from('generations')
+      .select('id')
+      .eq('id', basedOnGenerationId)
+      .maybeSingle();
+
+    if (basedOnError || !basedOnGen) {
+      basedOnGenerationId = null;
+    }
+  }
+
+  if (!basedOnGenerationId) {
+    const sourceImageUrl = typeof record.image === 'string' && record.image.length > 0
+      ? record.image
+      : null;
+    if (sourceImageUrl) {
+      basedOnGenerationId = await findSourceGenerationByImageUrl(supabase, sourceImageUrl);
+    }
+  }
+
+  return basedOnGenerationId;
+}

 /**
```

## Category 1: Component Decompositions

### GenerationsPane (547 lines removed from parent, ~960 added across new files)

The original `GenerationsPane.tsx` went from ~287 lines of imports + ~360 lines of component body down to ~61 lines. The logic was split into:
- `useGenerationsPaneController.ts` (281 lines) -- all the state/effects/callbacks
- `GenerationsPaneControls.tsx` (298 lines) -- the filter/pagination UI
- `GenerationsPaneGallery.tsx` (124 lines) -- the gallery rendering

**Verdict: Genuinely better.** The original was a 600+ line component mixing state management, pagination logic, filter UI, and gallery rendering. The controller hook cleanly separates concerns. The parent component is now a trivial composition. The extracted pieces have typed interfaces (e.g., `GenerationsPaneFiltersModel`, `GenerationsPanePaginationModel`). The total line count grew because of new typed interfaces and new test files, but the complexity per file dropped significantly.

### JoinClipsSettingsForm (645 deleted from parent, ~1080 added across new files)

Original shrank from ~817 lines to ~172. Extracted 5 sub-components plus a controller hook.

**Verdict: Genuinely better.** An 817-line form component with mixed concerns is a real maintenance problem. The extracted pieces (`JoinClipsStructureSettings` at 420 lines, `JoinClipsPromptSettings` at 117 lines) are domain-meaningful sections of the form. Net line growth is because of new tests and typed interfaces, which is acceptable.

### StrokeOverlay (extracting canvas + mask export)

`StrokeOverlay.tsx` lost ~150 lines. A new `StrokeOverlayCanvas.tsx` (182 lines) handles the Konva rendering, and `maskExport.ts` (107 lines) handles the mask export logic. The mask export also got named constants (`MASK_BACKGROUND`, `RECTANGLE_MASK_STROKE_WIDTH`) and a proper `finally` block for DOM cleanup.

**Verdict: Genuinely better.** This is a clean separation: business logic (drawing state machine) stays in StrokeOverlay, pure rendering goes to Canvas, and the export function (which was inline in an `useImperativeHandle`) becomes a standalone, testable pure function. The mask export also added proper tests (158 lines).

### PromptEditorModal (782 additions, 0 deletions)

This is suspicious. 782 lines added with nothing removed from a parent file. These are new component files and their tests but the parent file was never modified.

**Verdict: Neutral to concerning.** Without the parent shrinking, these extractions are additive code. They may be preparing for a future refactor of the parent, or they may be dead code that never gets wired in. This needs scrutiny -- if the parent was never touched, the new files might not even be imported anywhere.

### Overall Category 1 Assessment

3 out of 4 are genuine improvements (parent got meaningfully smaller, concerns were separated along domain boundaries). 1 (PromptEditorModal) is questionable because the parent was never changed.

## Category 2: "Fix" Commits -- Dead Code Removal in hooks/lib

### `useSpecificResources.ts` -- Removed dead `useInvalidateResource` hook

```typescript
// REMOVED:
const useInvalidateResource = () => {
  const queryClient = useQueryClient();
  return useCallback((resourceId: string) => {
    queryClient.removeQueries({ [REDACTED](resourceId) });
  }, [queryClient]);
};
void useInvalidateResource; // "Keep for potential future use"
```

**Verdict: Genuinely better.** The `void` trick to suppress unused-variable warnings while keeping dead code is a code smell. The function wasn't exported and had no callers. Removing it also removed the unused `useQueryClient` and `useCallback` imports.

### `aspectRatios.ts` -- Removed dead `getDisplayDimensions` function

Removed a 30-line function marked `@internal Not currently used externally` that was being kept alive with `void getDisplayDimensions`.

**Verdict: Genuinely better.** Same pattern -- dead code kept alive with `void`. Clean removal.

### `useLiveRelativeTimestamp.ts` -- Removed `void updateTrigger`

Tiny change: removed `void updateTrigger;` from a `useMemo`. The `updateTrigger` is already in the dependency array, so the `void` statement was doing nothing.

**Verdict: Genuinely better, though trivial.** The `void` was misleading -- it suggested `updateTrigger` needed to be "used" inside the memo body, but it was only needed as a dependency.

### `useGenerationInvalidation.ts` -- Fixed variant invalidation coalescing bug

This is the most substantive change in this category. The `waitForVariantDelay` function previously returned `void` and called all superseded settle callbacks with no indication they were superseded. Now it returns `boolean` -- `true` means "proceed with invalidation", `false` means "you were superseded, skip." The caller (`invalidateVariantChange`) now checks the return value and early-returns if superseded.

Before: when rapid variant changes coalesced, ALL callers would eventually run their invalidation logic, even the superseded ones, causing stale queries. Now: only the latest caller actually invalidates.

**Verdict: This is a real bug fix.** Not just cleanup -- this prevents redundant/stale cache invalidations during rapid variant switching. This is the kind of change that could fix subtle UI flickering or stale data issues.

### Overall Category 2 Assessment

Real cleanups. The dead code removals are legitimate (not "moving stuff around"), and the invalidation fix is a genuine bug fix. No busywork here.

---

## Category 3: Supabase Edge Function Changes

### `edgeHandler.ts` -- Structured error responses + `withEdgeRequest` pattern

Added `NO_SESSION_RUNTIME_OPTIONS` constant (DRY for 4+ edge functions that all had the same `auth: { autoRefreshToken: false, persistSession: false }` block). Added `deriveErrorCode` to convert freeform error strings into machine-readable codes. Changed `buildErrorResponse` from returning raw JSON `{ error: message }` to using `edgeErrorResponse` with `{ errorCode, message, recoverable }`.

**Verdict: Genuinely better.** This is moving from unstructured error responses to structured ones. A client can now programmatically check `errorCode` and `recoverable` instead of parsing error message strings. The `NO_SESSION_RUNTIME_OPTIONS` constant eliminates ~7 lines of boilerplate per function.

### `rateLimit.ts` -- Added `enforceRateLimit` convenience function

The existing rate limit code required callers to (1) call `checkRateLimit`, (2) check `isRateLimitExceededFailure`, (3) call `rateLimitFailureResponse`, (4) handle `fail_open` degraded mode. The new `enforceRateLimit` wraps all of this into one call that returns `Response | null`.

**Verdict: Genuinely better.** Reduces ~20 lines of rate limit boilerplate per edge function to a single function call. The implementation handles all edge cases (exceeded, service failure, degraded/fail_open) that callers were previously duplicating.

### `complete_task/index.ts` -- Error resilience + follow-up issue tracking

Added `markTaskFailed` (best-effort set task to "Failed" on unrecoverable errors), `persistCompletionFollowUpIssues` (record degraded post-completion steps without losing the generation), `completeTaskErrorResponse` (structured errors), and `resolveBasedOn` in params.ts (DB-verified `based_on` with image URL fallback).

The `resolveBasedOn` function is notable: it verifies the `based_on` generation actually exists in the DB before using it, and falls back to finding the source generation by image URL if the ID is stale. This handles a real edge case where generations can be deleted between task creation and completion.

**Verdict: Genuinely better.** These are real robustness improvements to the most critical edge function. The `markTaskFailed` pattern ensures the UI shows failure instead of leaving tasks stuck in "In Progress" forever. The follow-up issue tracking lets non-critical post-completion steps (cost calculation, orchestrator notification) fail gracefully without losing the generation.

### `claim-next-task/index.ts` -- Flattened nesting

The main change is switching from `bootstrapEdgeHandler` (result pattern) to `withEdgeRequest` (callback pattern), and removing one level of try/catch nesting. The logic is identical but reads more linearly.

**Verdict: Mildly better.** The de-nesting is real but modest. The `withEdgeRequest` pattern is arguably cleaner than the `if (!bootstrap.ok) return bootstrap.response` boilerplate.

### Overall Category 3 Assessment

These are the strongest changes on the branch. Structured error responses, rate limit consolidation, failure resilience in complete_task, and `based_on` verification are all real engineering improvements that address production reliability concerns.

---

## Category 4: The "repositories" Pattern

### `generationMutationsRepository.ts` (99 lines)

Contains 6 functions: `updateGenerationLocationByScope`, `createGenerationRecord`, `createGenerationPrimaryVariant`, `updateGenerationStarByScope`, `deleteGenerationByScope`, `deleteGenerationVariantByScope`.

Each function is essentially a typed wrapper around a single Supabase query:

```typescript
export function deleteGenerationByScope(params: GenerationSettingsInput) {
  return getSupabaseClient()
    .from('generations')
    .delete()
    .eq('id', params.id)
    .eq('project_id', params.projectId)
    .select('id');
}
```

**Verdict: Marginal.** These are thin wrappers around single DB calls. The typed input interfaces (`GenerationSettingsInput`, `DeleteGenerationVariantInput`) add a small amount of safety, and centralizing the scope-check pattern (`.eq('project_id', params.projectId)`) prevents callers from forgetting the project scope. But each function is 4-8 lines of implementation -- this is a lot of ceremony for simple operations.

The test file (151 lines) is testing that the Supabase client methods are called with the right arguments, which is basically testing the implementation rather than behavior.

**Overall Category 4 Assessment:** Low-value abstraction. The pattern isn't harmful, but the ROI is low. It adds indirection without adding meaningful safety beyond what TypeScript already provides at call sites. If these had complex query logic, transactions, or retry policies, the abstraction would pay for itself. As single-call wrappers, it's mostly ceremony.

---

## Category 5: Reverted Type-Splits

### What was reverted

Two commits reverted a total of 64 bot-applied interface splits. The pattern being reverted was: taking a flat props interface like:

```typescript
interface UseImg2ImgModeParams {
  media: Generation;
  selectedProjectId: string;
  sourceUrlForTasks: string;
  toolTypeOverride: string;
  // ...15 more fields
}
```

...and splitting it into sub-interfaces:

```typescript
interface Img2ImgStateParams { strength: number; setStrength: ...; /* etc */ }
interface Img2ImgSourceParams { baseImageUrl: string; /* etc */ }
interface UseImg2ImgModeParams {
  media: Generation;
  selectedProjectId: string;
  state: Img2ImgStateParams;
  source: Img2ImgSourceParams;
  options: Img2ImgOptionsParams;
}
```

### What was kept

The reverts explicitly kept interface restructuring on **large interfaces (30+ props)** where the groupings had domain meaning: `VideoPortionEditor`, `EditModePanel`, `WorkflowControlsBar`, `MediaLightbox`, `ImageLightbox`, `VideoEditPanel`. Also kept: `useImg2ImgMode` and `useLightboxVideoMode` (the example above) where the groupings represented genuinely different concerns (state vs source vs options).

### What was reverted

Interfaces with fewer than ~20 fields where the sub-interfaces were never reused and the grouping was arbitrary (e.g., splitting `ShotSelectorProps` into `ShotSelectorDataProps` and `ShotSelectorBehaviorProps` when there's only one consumer).

**Verdict: The reverts are correct.** The bot-applied type splits on small interfaces added naming overhead without reuse benefit. The commit messages show careful discrimination: they kept splits that improved large/complex interfaces and reverted splits that were pure noise. The first revert also fixed a real bug (toast dep arrays in `useShotActions`) and deleted dead code (`BrushStroke` duplicate, `_TransactionsSectionProps`).

---

## Overall Honest Assessment

**The branch is genuinely improving code quality, with some filler.**

**Strong wins (real engineering):**
- Edge function hardening (structured errors, rate limit consolidation, `markTaskFailed`, `resolveBasedOn`) -- these address production reliability
- The invalidation coalescing bug fix -- prevents stale cache data
- Dead code removal (the `void keepAlive` pattern was pervasive and is now cleaned up)
- The type-split reverts show good editorial judgment (keeping good bot work, reverting noise)
- Component decompositions for GenerationsPane, JoinClipsSettingsForm, and StrokeOverlay are genuine concern separation

**Neutral/filler:**
- The repositories pattern is low-value abstraction for single-call wrappers
- PromptEditorModal extractions appear to be additions without corresponding parent changes (need to verify if the parent was already small, or if this is dead code)
- Some of the test additions test implementation details rather than behavior

**Nothing is actively worse.** I didn't find any changes that make the code harder to understand, introduce new bugs, or are misleading. The worst items are just low-ROI, not harmful.

Rough breakdown: ~60% strong improvements, ~30% moderate/real-but-modest improvements, ~10% low-value ceremony. That's a solid ratio for a cleanup branch.

```
    10→import type { TimelineCoreResult } from './useTimelineCore.types';
    11→
    12→type InvalidateGenerationsFn = ReturnType<typeof useInvalidateGenerations>;
    13→
    14→type TimelinePairOperations = Pick<
    15→  TimelineCoreResult,
    16→  | 'pairPrompts'
    17→  | 'updatePairPrompts'
    18→  | 'updatePairPromptsByIndex'
    19→  | 'getSegmentOverrides'
    20→  | 'updateSegmentOverrides'
    21→>;
    22→
    23→export function useTimelinePairOperations(
    24→  shotId: string | null,
    25→  positionedItems: GenerationRow[],
    26→  invalidateGenerations: InvalidateGenerationsFn,
    27→  queryClient: ReturnType<typeof useQueryClient>,
    28→): TimelinePairOperations {
    29→  const pairPrompts = useMemo<TimelineCoreResult['pairPrompts']>(() => {
    30→    if (positionedItems.length === 0) {
    31→      return {};
    32→    }
    33→
    34→    const promptsByPair: Record<number, { prompt: string; negativePrompt: string }> = {};
    35→    for (let index = 0; index < positionedItems.length - 1; index += 1) {
    36→      const firstItem = positionedItems[index];
    37→      const overrides = readSegmentOverrides(firstItem.metadata as Record<string, unknown> | null);
    38→
    39→      if (overrides.prompt || overrides.negativePrompt) {
    40→        promptsByPair[index] = {
    41→          prompt: overrides.prompt || '',
    42→          negativePrompt: overrides.negativePrompt || '',
    43→        };
    44→      }
    45→    }
    46→
    47→    return promptsByPair;
    48→  }, [positionedItems]);
    49→
    50→  const updatePairPrompts = useCallback<TimelineCoreResult['updatePairPrompts']>(
    51→    async (shotGenerationId, prompt, negativePrompt) => {
    52→      if (!shotId) {
    53→        return;
    54→      }
    55→
    56→      try {
    57→        const item = positionedItems.find((generation) => generation.shotImageEntryId === shotGenerationId);
    58→        if (!item) {
    59→          throw new Error(`Item ${shotGenerationId} not found`);
    60→        }
    61→
    62→        const currentOverrides = readSegmentOverrides(item.metadata as Record<string, unknown> | null);
    63→        const updatedMetadata = writeSegmentOverrides(item.metadata as Record<string, unknown> | null, {
    64→          ...currentOverrides,
    65→          prompt,
    66→          negativePrompt,
    67→        });
    68→        const { error } = await supabase().from('shot_generations')
    69→          .update({ metadata: toJson(updatedMetadata) })
    70→          .eq('id', shotGenerationId);
    71→
    72→        if (error) {
    73→          throw error;
    74→        }
    75→        invalidateGenerations(shotId, { reason: 'update-pair-prompts', scope: 'metadata' });
    76→        queryClient.invalidateQueries({ [REDACTED](shotGenerationId) });
    77→      } catch (err) {
    78→        throw normalizeAndPresentError(err, {
    79→          context: 'useTimelineCore.updatePairPrompts',
    80→          toastTitle: 'Failed to update pair prompts',
    81→          showToast: false,
    82→        });
    83→      }
    84→    },
    85→    [shotId, positionedItems, invalidateGenerations, queryClient],
    86→  );
    87→
    88→  const updatePairPromptsByIndex = useCallback<TimelineCoreResult['updatePairPromptsByIndex']>(
    89→    async (pairIndex, prompt, negativePrompt) => {
    90→      if (pairIndex >= positionedItems.length - 1) {
    91→        return;
    92→      }
    93→
    94→      const firstItem = positionedItems[pairIndex];
    95→      if (!firstItem.shotImageEntryId) {
    96→        return;
    97→      }
    98→      await updatePairPrompts(firstItem.shotImageEntryId, prompt, negativePrompt);
    99→    },
   100→    [positionedItems, updatePairPrompts],
   101→  );
   102→
   103→  const getSegmentOverrides = useCallback<TimelineCoreResult['getSegmentOverrides']>(
   104→    (pairIndex) => {
   105→      if (pairIndex >= positionedItems.length - 1) {
   106→        return {};
   107→      }
   108→
   109→      const firstItem = positionedItems[pairIndex];
   110→      return readSegmentOverrides(firstItem.metadata as Record<string, unknown> | null);
   111→    },
   112→    [positionedItems],
   113→  );
   114→
   115→  const updateSegmentOverrides = useCallback<TimelineCoreResult['updateSegmentOverrides']>(
   116→    async (pairIndex, overrides) => {
   117→      if (!shotId || pairIndex >= positionedItems.length - 1) {
   118→        return;
   119→      }
   120→
   121→      const firstItem = positionedItems[pairIndex];
   122→      if (!firstItem.shotImageEntryId) {
   123→        return;
   124→      }
   125→
   126→      try {
   127→        const currentOverrides = readSegmentOverrides(firstItem.metadata as Record<string, unknown> | null);
   128→        const updatedMetadata = writeSegmentOverrides(firstItem.metadata as Record<string, unknown> | null, {
   129→          ...currentOverrides,
   130→          ...overrides,
   131→        });
   132→        const { error } = await supabase().from('shot_generations')
   133→          .update({ metadata: toJson(updatedMetadata) })
   134→          .eq('id', firstItem.shotImageEntryId);
   135→
   136→        if (error) {
   137→          throw error;
   138→        }
   139→        invalidateGenerations(shotId, { reason: 'update-segment-overrides', scope: 'metadata' });
   140→      } catch (err) {
   141→        throw normalizeAndPresentError(err, {
   142→          context: 'useTimelineCore.updateSegmentOverrides',
   143→          toastTitle: 'Failed to update segment overrides',
   144→          showToast: false,
   145→        });
   146→      }
   147→    },
   148→    [shotId, positionedItems, invalidateGenerations],
   149→  );
   150→
   151→  return {
   152→    pairPrompts,
   153→    updatePairPrompts,
   154→    updatePairPromptsByIndex,
   155→    getSegmentOverrides,
   156→    updateSegmentOverrides,
   157→  };
   158→}
```

```
1→import type { CSSProperties } from 'react';
     2→import type { GenerationRow } from '@/domains/generation/types';
     3→import { TIMELINE_PADDING_OFFSET } from './constants';
     4→import { getAspectRatioStyle as getProjectAspectRatioStyle } from '@/shared/components/ShotImageManager/utils/image-utils';
     5→
     6→interface TimelineItemPositionInput {
     7→  timelineWidth: number;
     8→  fullMinFrames: number;
     9→  fullRange: number;
    10→  framePosition: number;
    11→  isDragging: boolean;
    12→  dragOffset: { x: number; y: number } | null;
    13→  originalFramePos: number;
    14→  currentDragFrame: number | null;
    15→}
    16→
    17→export function getTimelineItemAspectRatioStyle(
    18→  image: GenerationRow,
    19→  projectAspectRatio?: string,
    20→): CSSProperties {
    21→  let width = image.metadata?.width as number | undefined;
    22→  let height = image.metadata?.height as number | undefined;
    23→
    24→  if (!width || !height) {
    25→    const originalParams = image.metadata?.originalParams as Record<string, unknown> | undefined;
    26→    const orchestratorDetails = originalParams?.orchestrator_details as Record<string, unknown> | undefined;
    27→    const resolution = orchestratorDetails?.resolution as string | undefined;
    28→    if (resolution && resolution.includes('x')) {
    29→      const [w, h] = resolution.split('x').map(Number);
    30→      if (!Number.isNaN(w) && !Number.isNaN(h)) {
    31→        width = w;
    32→        height = h;
    33→      }
    34→    }
    35→  }
    36→
    37→  if (width && height) {
    38→    return { aspectRatio: `${width / height}` };
    39→  }
    40→
    41→  return getProjectAspectRatioStyle(projectAspectRatio);
    42→}
    43→
    44→export function getTimelineItemPosition({
    45→  timelineWidth,
    46→  fullMinFrames,
    47→  fullRange,
    48→  framePosition,
    49→  isDragging,
    50→  dragOffset,
    51→  originalFramePos,
    52→  currentDragFrame,
    53→}: TimelineItemPositionInput): { leftPercent: number; displayFrame: number } {
    54→  const effectiveWidth = timelineWidth - (TIMELINE_PADDING_OFFSET * 2);
    55→  const pixelPosition = TIMELINE_PADDING_OFFSET + ((framePosition - fullMinFrames) / fullRange) * effectiveWidth;
    56→
    57→  let finalX = pixelPosition;
    58→  if (isDragging && dragOffset) {
    59→    const originalPixel = TIMELINE_PADDING_OFFSET + ((originalFramePos - fullMinFrames) / fullRange) * effectiveWidth;
    60→    finalX = originalPixel + dragOffset.x;
    61→  }
    62→
    63→  const displayFrame = isDragging && currentDragFrame !== null ? currentDragFrame : framePosition;
    64→  const leftPercent = (finalX / timelineWidth) * 100;
    65→
    66→  return { leftPercent, displayFrame };
    67→}
    68→
```

```
    44→function getEnhancedPromptFromMetadata(metadata: unknown): string {
    45→  if (!metadata || typeof metadata !== 'object') {
    46→    return '';
    47→  }
    48→  const value = (metadata as { enhanced_prompt?: unknown }).enhanced_prompt;
    49→  return typeof value === 'string' ? value : '';
    50→}
    51→
    52→export const PairRegionsLayer: React.FC<PairRegionsLayerProps> = ({
    53→  images,
    54→  imagePositionsWithPending,
    55→  pairInfoWithPending,
    56→  pairPrompts,
    57→  defaultPrompt,
    58→  defaultNegativePrompt,

    60→  dragState,
```

## Overall Verdict: Mixed -- mostly real improvement, with one area that's borderline busywork.

The total changeset (excluding `.desloppify/` metadata) is roughly +1063/-5239 lines in modified files, plus ~5269 lines across 45 new files. Net result: the tracked code files got **smaller by ~170 lines total** while gaining more files. This is decomposition, not deletion. The question is whether the decomposition boundaries are meaningful.

---

## Area 1: MediaLightbox Hooks Decomposition -- MOSTLY GOOD, with caveats

**What happened:**
- `useSharedLightboxState.ts` (809 lines) was split into 4 domain-focused files under `hooks/orchestration/`: variants (87 lines), interaction (213 lines), presentation (199 lines), types (140+ lines)
- `useVideoEditing.ts` (546 lines) was split into `hooks/modes/`: core, types, selections, task payload
- `useEditSettingsPersistence.ts` (387 lines) and `useEditSettingsSync.ts` (182 lines) moved into `hooks/persistence/`
- `buildImageEditStateValue.ts` and `editSettingsTypes.ts` moved into `model/`
- `StrokeOverlay.tsx` (410 lines -> 115 lines) with drawing logic extracted to `useStrokeOverlayDrawing.ts`
- `ImageLightbox.tsx` shrank by extracting a new `useImageLightboxControllers` hook

**Are the boundaries meaningful?**
Yes, mostly. The split of `useSharedLightboxState` into variants/interaction/presentation reflects genuine domain separation -- variant loading is orthogonal to shot positioning, which is orthogonal to layout/navigation. The persistence extraction also makes sense as a concern group.

**Concerns:**
1. **Re-export shims everywhere.** There are 10 files that are single-line `export * from './subdirectory/...'` shims. This means every old import path still works, which is nice for compatibility, but it's 10 extra files that exist only to maintain backward compatibility. These should eventually be removed.

2. **The duplicate file concern was a false alarm.** Files like `hooks/useSharedLightboxState.variants.ts` are just `export * from './orchestration/useSharedLightboxState.variants'`. No actual code duplication.

3. **`useImageLightboxControllers` is a borderline extraction.** It is a 260-line file (`/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/shared/components/MediaLightbox/hooks/orchestration/useImageLightboxControllers.ts`) that just moves `useMemo`/`useCallback` wiring out of `ImageLightbox.tsx`. The code is identical -- same dependency arrays, same logic. `ImageLightbox.tsx` went from calling those callbacks directly to calling `controllers.actionController.handleDownload`. This is a lateral move: it reduced `ImageLightbox.tsx` by ~160 lines but created a new 260-line file with the same complexity. The parent component now has to understand an intermediate abstraction (`controllers.panelController.showPanel` vs the old `showPanel`). **Marginal improvement at best.**

4. **MediaLightbox.tsx prop API restructuring is genuinely good.** The old `MediaLightbox` had a flat props interface with ~30+ individual props. The new version groups them into `navigation`, `features`, `actions`, `shotWorkflow`, `videoProps` -- structured sub-objects. This eliminated a large amount of adapter code inside `MediaLightbox.tsx` (the component that used to destructure flat props into grouped objects). Every caller (ShotImageManager, TasksPane, DesktopLightboxOverlay, FinalVideoSection, etc.) was updated to pass grouped props directly. This is a real API improvement that makes the component contract clearer.

---

## Area 2: Timeline Decomposition -- GENUINELY GOOD

**What happened:**
- `useTimelinePositions.ts` (701 -> 114 lines) extracted into `timelinePositionOperations.ts` (344 lines), `timelinePositionSync.ts`, and `timelinePositionTypes.ts`
- `TimelineContainer.tsx` (794 -> 584 lines, -210) with JSX layers extracted to `PairRegionsLayer.tsx`, `TimelineItemsLayer.tsx`, `TimelineTrackPrelude.tsx`, `TrailingEndpointLayer.tsx`
- `TimelineItem.tsx` (566 -> 289 lines) with helpers in `TimelineItem.helpers.ts` (67 lines) and action buttons in `TimelineItemActionButtons.tsx` (173 lines)
- `GuidanceVideoStrip.tsx` (554 -> 439 lines) with types/functions extracted to `.types.ts`, preview portal and range controls to separate components

**Are the boundaries meaningful?**
Yes. The `useTimelinePositions` split is along a clear seam: sync-from-database vs write-to-database operations. The `timelinePositionOperations.ts` file (`/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/tools/travel-between-images/components/Timeline/hooks/timeline-core/timelinePositionOperations.ts`) is a self-contained module handling optimistic updates, rollback, and database persistence -- a coherent unit.

The `TimelineContainer` layer extractions (PairRegions, TimelineItems, TrailingEndpoint) follow the visual structure of the timeline. Each renders a distinct visual layer. This is good component decomposition.

`TimelineItemActionButtons` is a clean extraction of JSX that was inline in `TimelineItem`. It's purely presentational with clear props.

**No concerns here.** These are the strongest extractions in the changeset.

---

## Area 3: useTimelineCore Extraction -- GOOD

The split of `useTimelineCore.ts` (686 -> 373 lines) into `.pairOperations.ts` (159 lines) and `.enhancedPromptOperations.ts` plus `.types.ts` (69 lines) is straightforward. The pair operations (segment overrides, prompts) and enhanced prompt operations were independent function groups that shared no state with each other beyond the positioned items array. The extraction is mechanical but the seams are real.

---

## Area 4: timelineWriteQueue Changes -- GENUINELY GOOD (not just decomposition)

This is the most valuable change in the batch. It:
1. **Eliminated `runSerializedTaskWithTimeout`** -- a redundant timeout wrapper that duplicated what `runTimelineWriteWithTimeout` already does. The old code had two different timeout implementations; now there's one.
2. **Added `upstreamSignal` support** to `runTimelineWriteWithTimeout`, allowing callers to pass an `AbortSignal` that can cancel in-flight writes. This is a real capability improvement.
3. **Changed `runSerializedTimelineWrite`'s task signature** from `() => Promise<T>` to `(signal: AbortSignal) => Promise<T>`, threading abort signals through the write pipeline.

This is a net deletion of ~44 lines and a genuine architectural improvement. Two timeout mechanisms became one, and abort signal propagation was added.

---

## Area 5: Other Component Changes (ShotImageManager, TasksPane, etc.) -- MECHANICAL BUT CORRECT

These are all callers being updated to use the new grouped MediaLightbox props API. The changes are repetitive but necessary -- when you restructure a component's props, every caller must update. No new logic, no new abstractions, just adapter updates. One minor improvement: `parentGenerationIdOverride={state.segments.selectedParentId}` became `parentGenerationIdOverride={state.segments.selectedParentId || undefined}`, fixing a potential `null` vs `undefined` type issue.

---

## Concerning Patterns

1. **Over-indirection in MediaLightbox orchestration.** The new `useImageLightboxControllers` hook creates a `controllers` object with sub-objects (`variantController`, `actionController`, `shotController`, `panelController`), and the parent accesses them like `controllers.panelController.showPanel`. This adds a naming layer without reducing complexity. The callbacks are literally the same code in a different file.

2. **10 re-export shim files** in the MediaLightbox area. These exist purely for backward import compatibility. They add noise to the file tree. Either commit to the new paths (update importers) or don't move files.

3. **Directory depth is getting aggressive.** `src/shared/components/MediaLightbox/hooks/orchestration/useSharedLightboxState.variants.ts` is a 6-level path. Combined with the shim at `hooks/useSharedLightboxState.variants.ts`, finding the real code requires knowing which is the shim and which is the source.

4. **No dead code creation detected.** I checked for functions that might have been copied rather than moved. The old files are either shims or genuinely reduced. No duplication.

---

## Summary Scorecard

| Area | Verdict | Why |
|---|---|---|
| MediaLightbox prop restructuring | **Real improvement** | Grouped API is clearer, eliminates adapter boilerplate in MediaLightbox.tsx |
| MediaLightbox hook decomposition (shared state) | **Good** | Variants/interaction/presentation are real domain boundaries |
| MediaLightbox `useImageLightboxControllers` | **Borderline busywork** | Moves useMemo/useCallback to a different file, adds indirection, same complexity |
| StrokeOverlay extraction | **Good** | Drawing logic separated from rendering |
| Timeline position hook split | **Good** | Clean sync vs operations boundary |
| Timeline component layer extractions | **Good** | Visual layers match component boundaries |
| TimelineItem extraction | **Good** | Helpers + action buttons are clean separations |
| useTimelineCore split | **Good** | Independent operation groups correctly separated |
| timelineWriteQueue refactor | **Best change in the batch** | Eliminated duplication, added real capability (abort signals) |
| Re-export shims | **Technical debt** | 10 files that should be temporary |
| Caller updates (ShotImageManager, TasksPane, etc.) | **Mechanical, correct** | Necessary consequence of prop restructuring |

**Bottom line:** Roughly 85% of this is genuinely making the codebase simpler to navigate and maintain. The timeline work and the write queue refactor are unambiguously good. The MediaLightbox prop restructuring is good. The main weak spot is `useImageLightboxControllers`, which is just shuffling code between files within the same component, and the 10 re-export shims that should be cleaned up rather than left as permanent fixtures.

```typescript
}
```

The refactor deleted `runSerializedTaskWithTimeout` entirely (-44 lines) and made `runSerializedTimelineWrite` use `runTimelineWriteWithTimeout` instead. It also:
1. Changed the task signature from `() => Promise<T>` to `(signal: AbortSignal) => Promise<T>`
2. Added `upstreamSignal` support so parent abort signals propagate through the write pipeline
3. Callers in `useTimelineCore.ts` now receive and use the signal

**Verdict: Better.** Eliminated real duplication and added real capability. This is an actual improvement, not just moving code around.

---

## Problems Found

1. **10 re-export shim files.** Files like `hooks/useSharedLightboxState.variants.ts` containing only `export * from './orchestration/useSharedLightboxState.variants'`. These maintain backward import compatibility but add permanent file tree noise. They should either be cleaned up (update all importers to use the new paths) or documented as temporary.

2. **useImageLightboxControllers adds indirection without reducing complexity.** The 260-line file is a 1:1 code relocation from `ImageLightbox.tsx`. The parent trades local variable access for `controllers.panelController.showPanel` traversals. Net effect: more files, more indirection, same logic.

3. **Directory depth.** `src/shared/components/MediaLightbox/hooks/orchestration/useSharedLightboxState.variants.ts` is getting deep. The `hooks/` directory now has subdirectories `orchestration/`, `modes/`, `persistence/`, `reposition/`, `inpainting/`, plus shim files. Navigating this requires knowledge of which files are shims vs real code.

4. **GuidanceVideoStrip comment stripping.** The diff removes many explanatory comments (e.g., `// Calculate effective output range`, `// Device detection and active state`, `// Temporary visibility for tap frame preview`). These were lightweight but useful for understanding what each block does. Removing them doesn't make the code simpler -- it just makes it less documented.

---

## Bottom Line

**~85% of this is real improvement.** The MediaLightbox prop restructuring, the timeline decompositions, the useTimelineCore split, and especially the timelineWriteQueue refactor are all genuinely making things better. The weak spots are the `useImageLightboxControllers` extraction (lateral move), the re-export shims (should be temporary), and the removed comments. This is not busywork disguised as cleanup.

```
import React, { useState, useRef, useEffect, useCallback } from 'react';
import { Button } from '@/shared/components/ui/button';
import { Label } from '@/shared/components/ui/primitives/label';
import { Select, SelectContent, SelectItem, SelectTrigger, SelectValue } from '@/shared/components/ui/select';
import { Slider } from '@/shared/components/ui/slider';
import { Video, X, Images } from 'lucide-react';
import { toast } from '@/shared/components/ui/runtime/sonner';
import { normalizeAndPresentError } from '@/shared/lib/errorHandling/runtimeError';
import { uploadVideoToStorage, extractVideoMetadata, VideoMetadata } from '@/shared/lib/media/videoUploader';
import { ResourceBrowserModalBase } from '@/features/resources/components/ResourceBrowserModalBase';
import { useCreateResource, Resource, StructureVideoMetadata } from '@/shared/hooks/useResources';
import { getSupabaseClient as supabase } from '@/integrations/supabase/client';
import { useUserUIState } from '@/shared/hooks/useUserUIState';

interface BatchGuidanceVideoProps {
  shotId: string;
  projectId: string;
  videoUrl: string | null;
  videoMetadata: VideoMetadata | null;
  treatment: 'adjust' | 'clip';
  motionStrength: number;
  structureType?: 'uni3c' | 'flow' | 'canny' | 'depth';
  onVideoUploaded: (videoUrl: string | null, metadata: VideoMetadata | null, resourceId?: string) => void;
  onTreatmentChange: (treatment: 'adjust' | 'clip') => void;
  onMotionStrengthChange: (strength: number) => void;
  onStructureTypeChange?: (type: 'uni3c' | 'flow' | 'canny' | 'depth') => void;
  /** Uni3C end percent (only shown when structureType is 'uni3c') */
  uni3cEndPercent?: number;
  onUni3cEndPercentChange?: (value: number) => void;
  imageCount?: number; // Number of images in the batch
  timelineFramePositions?: number[]; // Actual frame positions from timeline
  readOnly?: boolean;
  /** Hide structure type and strength controls (when shown elsewhere like Structure section) */
  hideStructureSettings?: boolean;
}

export const BatchGuidanceVideo: React.FC<BatchGuidanceVideoProps> = ({
  shotId,
  projectId: _projectId,
  videoUrl,
  videoMetadata,
  treatment,
  onVideoUploaded,
  onTreatmentChange,
  timelineFramePositions = [],
  readOnly = false,
}) => {
  // ALL HOOKS MUST BE AT THE TOP - before any conditional returns
  const [isUploading, setIsUploading] = useState(false);
  const [uploadProgress, setUploadProgress] = useState(0);
  const [showBrowser, setShowBrowser] = useState(false);
  const [isDragging, setIsDragging] = useState(false);
  const fileInputRef = React.useRef<HTMLInputElement>(null);
  const dropZoneRef = React.useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  
  // Resource creation hook
  const createResource = useCreateResource();
  
  // Privacy defaults for new resources
  const { value: privacyDefaults } = useUserUIState('privacyDefaults', { resourcesPublic: true, generationsPublic: false });
  
  // Video scrubbing hooks (always called, even if not used)
  const videoRef = useRef<HTMLVideoElement>(null);
  const canvasRef = useRef<HTMLCanvasElement>(null);
  const [currentTimelineFrame, setCurrentTimelineFrame] = useState(0);

  // Calculate frame range based on timeline positions
  const minFrame = timelineFramePositions.length > 0 ? Math.min(...timelineFramePositions) : 0;
  const maxFrame = timelineFramePositions.length > 0 ? Math.max(...timelineFramePositions) : 0;
  const timelineFrames = maxFrame - minFrame + 1;
  const totalVideoFrames = videoMetadata?.total_frames || 0;
  
  // Calculate video coverage for clip mode
  const videoCoversFrames = treatment === 'clip' ? Math.min(totalVideoFrames, timelineFrames) : timelineFrames;
  const lastCoveredFrame = treatment === 'clip' ? minFrame + videoCoversFrames - 1 : maxFrame;
  const isFrameBeyondVideoCoverage = treatment === 'clip' && currentTimelineFrame > lastCoveredFrame;
  
  // Calculate adjust mode description (stretch/compress)
  const adjustModeDescription = (() => {
    if (totalVideoFrames === 0 || timelineFrames === 0) return '';
    
    if (totalVideoFrames > timelineFrames) {
      const framesToDrop = totalVideoFrames - timelineFrames;
      return `Your input video has ${totalVideoFrames} frame${totalVideoFrames === 1 ? '' : 's'} so we'll drop ${framesToDrop} frame${framesToDrop === 1 ? '' : 's'} to compress your guide video to the ${timelineFrames} frame${timelineFrames === 1 ? '' : 's'} your input images cover.`;
    } else if (totalVideoFrames < timelineFrames) {
      const framesToDuplicate = timelineFrames - totalVideoFrames;
      return `Your input video has ${totalVideoFrames} frame${totalVideoFrames === 1 ? '' : 's'} so we'll duplicate ${framesToDuplicate} frame${framesToDuplicate === 1 ? '' : 's'} to stretch your guide video to the ${timelineFrames} frame${timelineFrames === 1 ? '' : 's'} your input images cover.`;
    } else {
      return `Perfect! Your input video has ${timelineFrames} frame${timelineFrames === 1 ? '' : 's'}, matching your timeline exactly.`;
    }
  })();
  
  // Calculate clip mode description (as-is)
  const clipModeDescription = (() => {
    if (totalVideoFrames === 0 || timelineFrames === 0) return '';
    
    if (totalVideoFrames > timelineFrames) {
      const unusedFrames = totalVideoFrames - timelineFrames;
      return `Your video will guide all ${timelineFrames} frame${timelineFrames === 1 ? '' : 's'} of your timeline. The last ${unusedFrames} frame${unusedFrames === 1 ? '' : 's'} of your video (frame${unusedFrames === 1 ? '' : 's'} ${timelineFrames + 1}-${totalVideoFrames}) will be ignored.`;
    } else if (totalVideoFrames < timelineFrames) {
      const uncoveredFrames = timelineFrames - totalVideoFrames;
      return `Your video will guide the first ${totalVideoFrames} frame${totalVideoFrames === 1 ? '' : 's'} of your timeline. The last ${uncoveredFrames} frame${uncoveredFrames === 1 ? '' : 's'} (frame${uncoveredFrames === 1 ? '' : 's'} ${totalVideoFrames + 1}-${timelineFrames}) won't have video guidance.`;
    } else {
      return `Perfect! Your video length matches your timeline exactly (${timelineFrames} frame${timelineFrames === 1 ? '' : 's'}).`;
    }
  })();

  // Draw a specific timeline frame to the canvas
  const drawTimelineFrame = useCallback((timelineFrame: number) => {
    const video = videoRef.current;
    const canvas = canvasRef.current;
    if (!video || !canvas || !videoMetadata) return;

    // Map timeline frame to video frame based on treatment mode
    let videoFrame: number;
    
    if (treatment === 'adjust') {
      // Adjust mode: stretch/compress entire video to match timeline range
      const timelineRange = maxFrame - minFrame;
      const normalizedPosition = timelineRange > 0 ? (timelineFrame - minFrame) / timelineRange : 0;
      videoFrame = Math.floor(normalizedPosition * (videoMetadata.total_frames - 1));
    } else {
      // Clip mode: 1:1 mapping from timeline start, clamped to video length
      const offsetFromStart = timelineFrame - minFrame;
      videoFrame = Math.min(offsetFromStart, videoMetadata.total_frames - 1);
    }

    const fps = videoMetadata.frame_rate;
    
    // Validate frame_rate to prevent NaN/Infinity errors
    if (!fps || fps <= 0 || !isFinite(fps)) {
      console.error('[BatchGuidanceVideo] Invalid frame_rate:', fps);
      return;
    }
    
    const timeInSeconds = videoFrame / fps;
    
    // Additional safety check for currentTime value
    if (!isFinite(timeInSeconds) || timeInSeconds < 0) {
      console.error('[BatchGuidanceVideo] Invalid time value:', { videoFrame, fps, timeInSeconds });
      return;
    }

    video.currentTime = timeInSeconds;

    const handleSeeked = () => {
      const ctx = canvas.getContext('2d');
      if (!ctx) return;

      canvas.width = video.videoWidth;
      canvas.height = video.videoHeight;
      ctx.drawImage(video, 0, 0);

      video.removeEventListener('seeked', handleSeeked);
    };

    video.addEventListener('seeked', handleSeeked);
  }, [videoMetadata, treatment, minFrame, maxFrame]);

  // Handle slider change
  const handleFrameChange = useCallback((value: number) => {
    const newFrame = value;
    setCurrentTimelineFrame(newFrame);
    drawTimelineFrame(newFrame);
  }, [drawTimelineFrame]);

  // Load video and draw initial frame
  useEffect(() => {
    const video = videoRef.current;
    if (!video || !videoUrl) return;

    const handleLoadedMetadata = () => {
      drawTimelineFrame(minFrame);
    };

    video.addEventListener('loadedmetadata', handleLoadedMetadata);
    return () => video.removeEventListener('loadedmetadata', handleLoadedMetadata);
  }, [videoUrl, minFrame, drawTimelineFrame]);

  // Process uploaded file (shared by file input and drag-drop)
  const processFile = useCallback(async (file: File) => {
    // Validate file type
    const validTypes = ['video/mp4', 'video/webm', 'video/quicktime'];
    if (!validTypes.includes(file.type)) {
      toast.error('Invalid file type. Please upload an MP4, WebM, or MOV file.');
      return;
    }

    // Validate file size (max 200MB)
    const maxSizeMB = 200;
    const fileSizeMB = file.size / (1024 * 1024);
    if (fileSizeMB > maxSizeMB) {
      toast.error(`File too large. Maximum size is ${maxSizeMB}MB (file is ${fileSizeMB.toFixed(1)}MB)`);
      return;
    }

    try {
      setIsUploading(true);
      setUploadProgress(0);

      // Extract metadata
      const metadata = await extractVideoMetadata(file);
      setUploadProgress(25);

      // Upload to storage
      const uploadedVideoUrl = await uploadVideoToStorage(
        file,
        {
          onProgress: (progress) => setUploadProgress(25 + (progress * 0.65)), // Map 0-100 to 25-90
        }
      );
      setUploadProgress(90);

      // Create resource for reuse
      const { data: { user } } = await supabase().auth.getUser();
      const now = new Date().toISOString();
      const resourceMetadata: StructureVideoMetadata = {
        name: `Guidance Video ${new Date().toLocaleString()}`,
        videoUrl: uploadedVideoUrl,
        thumbnailUrl: null, // Could generate a thumbnail later
        videoMetadata: metadata,
        created_by: {
          is_you: true,
          username: user?.email || 'user',
        },
        is_public: privacyDefaults.resourcesPublic,
        createdAt: now,
      };
      
      const resource = await createResource.mutateAsync({
        type: 'structure-video',
        metadata: resourceMetadata,
      });
      setUploadProgress(100);

      // Notify parent with resource ID
      onVideoUploaded(uploadedVideoUrl, metadata, resource.id);
    } catch (error) {
      normalizeAndPresentError(error, { context: 'BatchGuidanceVideo', toastTitle: 'Failed to upload video' });
    } finally {
      setIsUploading(false);
      setUploadProgress(0);
      if (fileInputRef.current) {
        fileInputRef.current.value = '';
      }
    }
  }, [privacyDefaults.resourcesPublic, createResource, onVideoUploaded]);

  const handleFileSelect = async (event: React.ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement>) => {
    const file = event.target.files?.[0];
    if (!file) return;
    await processFile(file);
  };

  // Drag and drop handlers
  const handleDragEnter = useCallback((e: React.DragEvent) => {
    e.preventDefault();
    e.stopPropagation();
    if (!isUploading) {
      setIsDragging(true);
    }
  }, [isUploading]);

  const handleDragLeave = useCallback((e: React.DragEvent) => {
    e.preventDefault();
    e.stopPropagation();
    // Only set dragging to false if we're leaving the drop zone entirely
    if (dropZoneRef.current && !dropZoneRef.current.contains(e.relatedTarget as Node)) {
      setIsDragging(false);
    }
  }, []);

  const handleDragOver = useCallback((e: React.DragEvent) => {
    e.preventDefault();
    e.stopPropagation();
  }, []);

  const handleDrop = useCallback(async (e: React.DragEvent) => {
    e.preventDefault();
    e.stopPropagation();
    setIsDragging(false);

    if (isUploading) return;

    const files = e.dataTransfer.files;
    if (files.length > 0) {
      await processFile(files[0]);
    }
  }, [isUploading, processFile]);

  const handleRemoveVideo = () => {
    onVideoUploaded(null, null, undefined);
    if (fileInputRef.current) {
      fileInputRef.current.value = '';
    }
  };

  // Handle selecting a video from the browser
  const handleResourceSelect = useCallback((resource: Resource) => {
    const metadata = resource.metadata as StructureVideoMetadata;
    onVideoUploaded(metadata.videoUrl, metadata.videoMetadata, resource.id);
    setShowBrowser(false);
  }, [onVideoUploaded]);

  if (!videoUrl) {
    // In readOnly mode, don't show upload UI when there's no video
    if (readOnly) {
      return null;
    }

    // Upload prompt - responsive width with drag-drop support
    return (
      <>
        <div className="mb-4">
          <div
            ref={dropZoneRef}
            className={`w-full sm:w-2/3 md:w-1/2 lg:w-1/3 p-4 border-2 border-dashed rounded-lg transition-colors ${
              isDragging
                ? 'border-primary bg-primary/10'
                : 'border-border bg-muted/20 hover:border-muted-foreground/50'
            }`}
            onDragEnter={handleDragEnter}
            onDragLeave={handleDragLeave}
            onDragOver={handleDragOver}
            onDrop={handleDrop}
          >
            <div className="flex flex-col items-center gap-3 text-center">
              <Video className={`h-8 w-8 ${isDragging ? 'text-primary' : 'text-muted-foreground'}`} />
              <p className="text-xs text-muted-foreground">
                {isDragging
                  ? 'Drop video here'
                  : 'Add a motion guidance video to control the animation'}
              </p>

              <input
                ref={fileInputRef}
                type="file"
                accept="video/mp4,video/webm,video/quicktime"
                onChange={handleFileSelect}
                disabled={isUploading}
                className="hidden"
                id={`batch-video-upload-${shotId}`}
              />

              <div className="flex gap-2 w-full">
                <Label htmlFor={`batch-video-upload-${shotId}`} className="m-0 cursor-pointer flex-1">
                  <Button
                    variant="outline"
                    size="sm"
                    disabled={isUploading}
                    className="w-full"
                    asChild
                  >
                    <span>
                      {isUploading ? `Uploading... ${Math.round(uploadProgress)}%` : 'Upload'}
                    </span>
                  </Button>
                </Label>

                <Button
                  variant="outline"
                  size="sm"
                  disabled={isUploading}
                  onClick={() => setShowBrowser(true)}
                  className="flex-1"
                >
                  <Images className="h-4 w-4 mr-1" />
                  Browse
                </Button>
              </div>

              {isUploading && (
                <div className="w-full bg-muted rounded-full h-2">
                  <div
                    className="bg-primary h-2 rounded-full transition-all"
                    style={{ width: `${Math.round(uploadProgress)}%` }}
                  />
                </div>
              )}
            </div>
          </div>
        </div>

        <ResourceBrowserModalBase
          isOpen={showBrowser}
          onOpenChange={setShowBrowser}
          resourceType="structure-video"
          title="Browse Guidance Videos"
          onResourceSelect={handleResourceSelect}
        />
      </>
    );
  }

  // Video display with settings
  return (
    <div className="mb-4">
      <div className="border rounded-lg overflow-hidden bg-background">
        <div className="flex flex-col md:flex-row">
        {/* Video preview - top on mobile, left third on desktop */}
        <div className="w-full md:w-1/3 relative bg-black aspect-video flex-shrink-0 flex flex-col">
          {/* Hidden video element for seeking */}
          <video
            ref={videoRef}
            src={videoUrl}
            preload="metadata"
            className="hidden"
            muted
          />
          
          {/* Canvas to display current frame */}
          <canvas
            ref={canvasRef}
            className="w-full h-full object-contain"
          />
          
          {/* Overlay message when beyond video coverage */}
          {isFrameBeyondVideoCoverage && (
            <div className="absolute inset-0 flex items-center justify-center pointer-events-none">
              <div className="bg-black/80 text-white px-4 py-3 rounded-lg text-center max-w-[80%]">
                <p className="text-sm font-medium">
                  The guidance video only covers {videoCoversFrames} frame{videoCoversFrames === 1 ? '' : 's'}
                </p>
                <p className="text-xs text-white/70 mt-1">
                  (frames {minFrame}-{lastCoveredFrame})
                </p>
              </div>
            </div>
          )}
          
          {/* Frame scrubber at bottom */}
          <div className="absolute bottom-0 left-0 right-0 bg-black/80 p-2 space-y-1">
            <div className="flex items-center justify-between text-xs text-white/80">
              <span>Timeline Frame: {currentTimelineFrame}</span>
              <span>{minFrame} - {maxFrame}</span>
            </div>
            <Slider
              value={currentTimelineFrame}
              onValueChange={handleFrameChange}
              min={minFrame}
              max={maxFrame}
              step={1}
              className="w-full"
              disabled={readOnly}
            />
          </div>
        </div>

        {/* Remove Video button - below video on mobile only */}
        <div className="md:hidden p-3 border-t">
          {!readOnly && (
            <Button
              variant="outline"
              size="sm"
              className="w-full text-destructive hover:text-destructive hover:bg-destructive/10"
              onClick={handleRemoveVideo}
            >
              <X className="h-4 w-4 mr-2" />
              Remove Video
            </Button>
          )}
        </div>

        {/* Settings panel - below on mobile, right two thirds on desktop */}
        <div className="flex-1 p-4 bg-muted/20 flex flex-col gap-4">
          {/* Treatment mode */}
          <div className="space-y-2">
            <Label className="text-sm">How would you like to cut the guidance video to match the timeline?</Label>
            <div className="flex flex-col md:flex-row md:items-center gap-3">
              <div className="flex-shrink-0 w-full md:w-[200px]">
<Select value={treatment} onValueChange={onTreatmentChange} disabled={readOnly}>
                  <SelectTrigger variant="retro" size="sm" className="h-9 w-full">
                    <SelectValue>
                      {treatment === 'adjust'
                        ? (totalVideoFrames > timelineFrames ? 'Compress' : totalVideoFrames < timelineFrames ? 'Stretch' : 'Match') + ' to timeline'
                        : 'Use video as is'}
                    </SelectValue>
                  </SelectTrigger>
                  <SelectContent variant="retro">
                    <SelectItem variant="retro" value="adjust">
                      {totalVideoFrames > timelineFrames ? 'Compress' : totalVideoFrames < timelineFrames ? 'Stretch' : 'Match'} to timeline
                    </SelectItem>
                    <SelectItem variant="retro" value="clip">
                      Use video as is
                    </SelectItem>
                  </SelectContent>
                </Select>
              </div>
              <div className="flex-1 text-xs text-muted-foreground leading-relaxed">
                {treatment === 'adjust' ? adjustModeDescription : clipModeDescription}
              </div>
            </div>
          </div>

          {/* Delete button at bottom - desktop only */}
          <div className="mt-auto pt-2 hidden md:block">
            {!readOnly && (
              <Button
                variant="outline"
                size="sm"
                className="w-full text-destructive hover:text-destructive hover:bg-destructive/10"
                onClick={handleRemoveVideo}
              >
                <X className="h-4 w-4 mr-2" />
                Remove Video
              </Button>
            )}
          </div>
        </div>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  );
};
```
