```
                updateGenerationMethods({ inCloud: true, onComputer: false });
              } else if (value === 'local') {
                updateGenerationMethods({ onComputer: true, inCloud: false });
              }
            }}
            variant="pill"
          >
            <SegmentedControlItem value="cloud" colorScheme="blue">
              In the cloud ☁️
            </SegmentedControlItem>
            <SegmentedControlItem value="local" colorScheme="emerald">
              On my computer 💻
            </SegmentedControlItem>
          </SegmentedControl>
        </div>

        {/* Additional info below toggle */}
        <div className="text-center space-y-3">
          {inCloudChecked && !onComputerChecked && (
            <div className="p-4 bg-secondary/50 rounded-lg">
              <p className="text-sm text-secondary-foreground font-light">
                ☁️ Easy setup, pay-per-use, works on any device
              </p>
            </div>
          )}

          {onComputerChecked && !inCloudChecked && (
            <div className="p-4 bg-accent rounded-lg">
              <p className="text-sm text-accent-foreground font-light flex items-center justify-center gap-2">
                <span>💻 Free to use, requires setup, need a good GPU</span>
                <span className="bg-primary text-primary-foreground text-xs font-light px-2 py-1 rounded-full">Free</span>
              </p>
            </div>
          )}
        </div>

        {!onComputerChecked && !inCloudChecked && (
          <div className="text-center">
            <img
              src="https://[REDACTED]/storage/v1/object/public/image_uploads/files/ds.gif"
              alt="Choose generation method"
              className="w-[120px] h-[120px] object-contain transform scale-x-[-1] mx-auto"
            />
            <p className="text-sm text-muted-foreground mt-2">
              Select at least one option to continue
            </p>
          </div>
        )}
      </div>
      
      <div className="flex justify-center pt-5 pb-2">
        <Button 
          variant="retro"
          size="retro-sm"
          onClick={onNext} 
          disabled={!onComputerChecked && !inCloudChecked}
          className="w-full sm:w-auto"
        >
          Continue
          <ChevronRight className="w-4 h-4 ml-2" />
        </Button>
      </div>
    </>
  );
};

// Step 4: Theme Selection
const ThemeStep: React.FC<{ onNext: () => void }> = ({ onNext }) => {
  const colors = getStepColors(4);
  const { darkMode, setDarkMode } = useDarkMode();
  
  // Also persist to database for cross-device sync
  const { 
    update: updateThemePreference 
  } = useUserUIState('theme', { darkMode: true });

  const handleThemeChange = (isDark: boolean) => {
    setDarkMode(isDark);
    updateThemePreference({ darkMode: isDark });
  };

  return (
    <>
      <DialogHeader className="text-center space-y-4 mb-6">
        <div className={`mx-auto w-16 h-16 ${colors.bg} rounded-full flex items-center justify-center`}>
          {darkMode ? (
            <Moon className={`w-8 h-8 ${colors.icon}`} />
          ) : (
            <Sun className={`w-8 h-8 ${colors.icon}`} />
          )}
        </div>
        <DialogTitle className="text-2xl font-bold text-center">
          Choose Your Theme
        </DialogTitle>
      </DialogHeader>
      
      <div className="space-y-6">
        <p className="text-center text-muted-foreground">
          Which mode do you prefer? You can always change this later in settings.
        </p>

        <div className="flex justify-center px-4">
          <SegmentedControl
            value={darkMode ? 'dark' : 'light'}
            onValueChange={(value) => handleThemeChange(value === 'dark')}
            variant="pill"
          >
            <SegmentedControlItem value="light" colorScheme="amber" icon={<Sun className="h-4 w-4" />}>
              Light
            </SegmentedControlItem>
            <SegmentedControlItem value="dark" colorScheme="violet" icon={<Moon className="h-4 w-4" />}>
              Dark
            </SegmentedControlItem>
          </SegmentedControl>
        </div>

      </div>
      
      <div className="flex justify-center pt-5 pb-2">
        <Button variant="retro" size="retro-sm" onClick={onNext} className="w-full sm:w-auto">
          Continue
          <ChevronRight className="w-4 h-4 ml-2" />
        </Button>
      </div>
    </>
  );
};

// Step 5: Privacy Defaults
const PrivacyDefaultsStep: React.FC<{ onNext: () => void }> = ({ onNext }) => {
  const colors = getStepColors(5);
  
  // Privacy defaults state using database-backed preferences
  const { 
    value: privacyDefaults, 
    update: updatePrivacyDefaults,
    isLoading: isLoadingPrivacyDefaults
  } = useUserUIState('privacyDefaults', { resourcesPublic: true, generationsPublic: false });

  if (isLoadingPrivacyDefaults) {
    return (
      <>
        <DialogHeader className="text-center space-y-4 mb-6">
          <div className={`mx-auto w-16 h-16 ${colors.bg} rounded-full flex items-center justify-center`}>
            <Globe className={`w-8 h-8 ${colors.icon}`} />
          </div>
          <DialogTitle className="text-2xl font-bold text-center">
            Privacy Defaults
          </DialogTitle>
        </DialogHeader>
        <div className="flex justify-center py-8">
          <Loader2 className="w-8 h-8 animate-spin text-muted-foreground" />
        </div>
      </>
    );
  }

  return (
    <>
      <DialogHeader className="text-center space-y-4 mb-6">
        <div className={`mx-auto w-16 h-16 ${colors.bg} rounded-full flex items-center justify-center`}>
          <Globe className={`w-8 h-8 ${colors.icon}`} />
        </div>
        <DialogTitle className="text-2xl font-bold text-center">
          Are you okay with your creations being public?
        </DialogTitle>
      </DialogHeader>
      
      <div className="space-y-4">
        {/* Side by side toggles */}
        <div className="grid grid-cols-2 gap-3">
          {/* Resources Toggle */}
          <div className="p-3 bg-muted/50 rounded-lg space-y-2">
            <span className="font-medium text-sm">Resources</span>
            <p className="text-xs text-muted-foreground leading-snug">
              This will allow others to use them. You can update this for individual resources.
            </p>
            <PrivacyToggle
              isPublic={privacyDefaults.resourcesPublic}
              onValueChange={(isPublic) => updatePrivacyDefaults({ resourcesPublic: isPublic })}
              size="sm"
            />
          </div>

          {/* Generations Toggle */}
          <div className="p-3 bg-muted/50 rounded-lg space-y-2">
            <span className="font-medium text-sm">Generations</span>
            <p className="text-xs text-muted-foreground leading-snug">
              This will allow others to view your generations, and train LoRAs on them.
            </p>
            <PrivacyToggle
              isPublic={privacyDefaults.generationsPublic}
              onValueChange={(isPublic) => updatePrivacyDefaults({ generationsPublic: isPublic })}
              size="sm"
            />
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>
      
      <div className="flex justify-center pt-5 pb-2">
        <Button variant="retro" size="retro-sm" onClick={onNext} className="w-full sm:w-auto">
          Continue
          <ChevronRight className="w-4 h-4 ml-2" />
        </Button>
      </div>
    </>
);
};

// Step 6: Setup Complete
const SetupCompleteStep: React.FC<{ onClose: () => void }> = ({ onClose }) => {
  const colors = getStepColors(6);
  
  const handleOpenSettings = () => {
    onClose();
    // Trigger settings modal to open - we'll need to communicate this back to the parent
    setTimeout(() => {
      // This is a bit hacky, but we can trigger a custom event or use a callback
      dispatchAppEvent('openSettings', { tab: 'generate-locally' });
    }, 100);
  };

  return (
    <>
      <DialogHeader className="text-center space-y-4 mb-6">
        <div className={`mx-auto w-16 h-16 ${colors.bg} rounded-full flex items-center justify-center`}>
        <MoreHorizontal className={`w-8 h-8 ${colors.icon}`} />
        </div>
        <DialogTitle className="text-2xl font-bold text-center">
          One more thing
        </DialogTitle>
      </DialogHeader>
      
      <div className="text-center space-y-4">
        <p className="text-muted-foreground">
          Reigh is an early-stage tool. If there's anything that isn't working for you or could be better, please drop into our Discord and leave a message in our #support channel or DM POM.
        </p>
        <p className="text-muted-foreground">
          There's no feedback too big or too small - so please share!
        </p>
      </div>
      
      <div className="flex flex-col gap-y-2 pt-5 pb-2">
        <Button variant="retro" size="retro-sm" onClick={handleOpenSettings} className="w-full">
          <Settings className="w-4 h-4 mr-2" />
          Open Settings to Get Set Up
        </Button>
        <Button variant="retro-secondary" size="retro-sm" onClick={onClose} className="w-full">
          Start Creating
        </Button>
      </div>
    </>
  );
};

export const OnboardingModal: React.FC<OnboardingModalProps> = ({
  isOpen,
  onClose,
}) => {
  const [currentStep, setCurrentStep] = useState(1);
  const [isShaking, setIsShaking] = useState(false);
  const shakeTimeoutRef = useRef<ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | null>(null);
  const modal = useMediumModal();
  const { showFade, scrollRef } = useScrollFade({
    isOpen,
    preloadFade: modal.isMobile
  });

  // Reset to step 1 when modal opens
  useEffect(() => {
    if (isOpen) {
      setCurrentStep(1);
    }
  }, [isOpen]);

  // Cleanup shake timeout on unmount
  useEffect(() => {
    return () => {
      if (shakeTimeoutRef.current) {
        clearTimeout(shakeTimeoutRef.current);
      }
    };
  }, []);

  const handleNext = () => {
    setCurrentStep(prev => Math.min(prev + 1, 6));
  };

  const handleBack = () => {
    setCurrentStep(prev => Math.max(prev - 1, 1));
  };

  const handleShake = () => {
    setIsShaking(true);
    if (shakeTimeoutRef.current) {
      clearTimeout(shakeTimeoutRef.current);
    }
    shakeTimeoutRef.current = setTimeout(() => setIsShaking(false), 500);
  };

  // Render current step component conditionally to avoid calling hooks for unused steps
  const renderCurrentStep = () => {
    switch (currentStep) {
      case 1:
        return <IntroductionStep onNext={handleNext} />;
      case 2:
        return <CommunityStep onNext={handleNext} />;
      case 3:
        return <GenerationMethodStep onNext={handleNext} />;
      case 4:
        return <ThemeStep onNext={handleNext} />;
      case 5:
        return <PrivacyDefaultsStep onNext={handleNext} />;
      case 6:
        return <SetupCompleteStep onClose={onClose} />;
      default:
        return <IntroductionStep onNext={handleNext} />;
    }
  };

  const stepTitles = ["Welcome", "Community", "Generation", "Theme", "Privacy", "Complete"];
  
  return (
    <Dialog open={isOpen} onOpenChange={handleShake}>
      <DialogContent 
        className={modal.className}
        style={modal.style}
      >
        <style>
          {`
            @keyframes shake {
              0%, 100% { transform: translateX(0); }
              10%, 30%, 50%, 70%, 90% { transform: translateX(-8px); }
              20%, 40%, 60%, 80% { transform: translateX(8px); }
            }
            .shake-wrapper {
              animation: shake 0.5s ease-in-out;
            }
          `}
        </style>
        <style>{`
          /* Hide the built-in close button from Dialog component */
          button[data-dialog-close] {
            display: none !important;
          }
        `}</style>
        <div className={`flex flex-col flex-1 min-h-0 ${isShaking ? 'shake-wrapper' : ''}`}>
          <div className={modal.headerClass}></div>

        <div ref={scrollRef} className={modal.scrollClass}>
          {renderCurrentStep()}
          <div className="h-6"></div>
        </div>
        
        <div className={`${modal.footerClass} relative`}>
          {/* Fade overlay */}
          {showFade && (
            <div 
              className="absolute top-0 left-0 right-0 h-16 pointer-events-none z-10"
              style={{ transform: 'translateY(-64px)' }}
            >
              <div className="h-full bg-gradient-to-t from-card via-card/95 to-transparent" />
            </div>
          )}

          {/* Step indicator and back button container */}
          <div className="relative flex justify-center gap-x-2 pt-6 pb-2 border-t relative z-20">
            {/* Back button - only show after step 1 */}
            {currentStep > 1 && (
              <button
                onClick={handleBack}
                className="absolute left-0 top-1/2 -translate-y-1/4 rounded-sm opacity-70 ring-offset-background transition-opacity hover:opacity-100 focus:outline-none focus:ring-2 focus:ring-ring focus:ring-offset-2 flex items-center gap-x-1 text-sm text-muted-foreground hover:text-foreground"
              >
                <ChevronLeft className="h-4 w-4" />
                <span>Back</span>
              </button>
            )}
            
            {/* Step indicators */}
            <div className="flex gap-x-2">
              {stepTitles.map((_, index) => (
                <div 
                  key={index}
                  className={`w-2 h-2 rounded-full transition-colors ${
                    currentStep === index + 1 ? 'bg-primary' : 'bg-muted'
                  }`}
                />
              ))}
            </div>
            </div>
          </div>
        </div>
      </DialogContent>
    </Dialog>
  );
};
```

```
    91→
    92→  const handleCopyInstallCommand = async () => {
```

```
1→import { useCallback, useEffect, useState } from 'react';
     2→import { dispatchAppEvent } from '@/shared/lib/typedEvents';
     3→
     4→interface UseMobileImageSelectionParams {
     5→  readOnly: boolean;
     6→  onSelectionChange?: (hasSelection: boolean) => void;
     7→}
     8→
     9→export function useMobileImageSelection({
    10→  readOnly,
    11→  onSelectionChange,
    12→}: UseMobileImageSelectionParams) {
    13→  const [mobileSelectedIds, setMobileSelectedIds] = useState<string[]>([]);
    14→  const [showSelectionBar, setShowSelectionBar] = useState(false);
    15→
    16→  const isInMoveMode = mobileSelectedIds.length > 0;
    17→
    18→  useEffect(() => {
    19→    if (mobileSelectedIds.length > 0) {
    20→      const timer = setTimeout(() => {
    21→        setShowSelectionBar(true);
    22→      }, 200);
    23→      return () => clearTimeout(timer);
    24→    }
    25→    setShowSelectionBar(false);
    26→  }, [mobileSelectedIds.length]);
    27→
    28→  useEffect(() => {
    29→    const hasSelection = mobileSelectedIds.length > 0;
    30→    dispatchAppEvent('mobileSelectionActive', hasSelection);
    31→    onSelectionChange?.(hasSelection);
    32→
    33→    return () => {
    34→      dispatchAppEvent('mobileSelectionActive', false);
    35→    };
    36→  }, [mobileSelectedIds.length, onSelectionChange]);
    37→
    38→  const handleMobileTap = useCallback(
    39→    (imageId: string, _index?: number) => {
    40→      if (readOnly) {
    41→        return;
    42→      }
    43→
    44→      const wasSelected = mobileSelectedIds.includes(imageId);
    45→      if (wasSelected) {
    46→        setMobileSelectedIds((previous) =>
    47→          previous.filter((id) => id !== imageId)
    48→        );
    49→      } else {
    50→        setMobileSelectedIds((previous) => [...previous, imageId]);
    51→      }
    52→    },
    53→    [mobileSelectedIds, readOnly]
    54→  );
    55→
    56→  const clearSelection = useCallback(() => {
    57→    setMobileSelectedIds([]);
    58→    onSelectionChange?.(false);
    59→  }, [onSelectionChange]);
    60→
    61→  return {
    62→    mobileSelectedIds,
    63→    setMobileSelectedIds,
    64→    showSelectionBar,
    65→    isInMoveMode,
    66→    handleMobileTap,
    67→    clearSelection,
    68→  };
    69→}
    70→
```

```
1→import { useEffect, useRef, useState } from 'react';
     2→import type { GenerationRow } from '@/domains/generation/types';
     3→
     4→export function useMobileOptimisticOrder(images: GenerationRow[]) {
     5→  const [optimisticOrder, setOptimisticOrder] = useState<GenerationRow[]>([]);
     6→  const [isOptimisticUpdate, setIsOptimisticUpdate] = useState(false);
     7→
     8→  const currentImages =
     9→    isOptimisticUpdate && optimisticOrder.length > 0 ? optimisticOrder : images;
    10→
    11→  const prevImagesLengthRef = useRef(images.length);
    12→  useEffect(() => {
    13→    const lengthDiff = Math.abs(images.length - prevImagesLengthRef.current);
    14→    if (lengthDiff > 1 && isOptimisticUpdate) {
    15→      setIsOptimisticUpdate(false);
    16→      setOptimisticOrder([]);
    17→    }
    18→    prevImagesLengthRef.current = images.length;
    19→  }, [images.length, isOptimisticUpdate]);
    20→
    21→  useEffect(() => {
    22→    if (isOptimisticUpdate && images.length > 0) {
    23→      const optimisticIds = optimisticOrder.map((image) => image.id).join(',');
    24→      const serverIds = images.map((image) => image.id).join(',');
    25→
    26→      if (optimisticIds === serverIds) {
    27→        setIsOptimisticUpdate(false);
    28→        setOptimisticOrder([]);
    29→      } else {
    30→        const timeout = setTimeout(() => {
    31→          if (isOptimisticUpdate) {
    32→            setIsOptimisticUpdate(false);
    33→            setOptimisticOrder([]);
    34→          }
    35→        }, 5000);
    36→        return () => clearTimeout(timeout);
    37→      }
    38→    }
    39→  }, [images, isOptimisticUpdate, optimisticOrder]);
    40→
    41→  return {
    42→    currentImages,
    43→    optimisticOrder,
    44→    setOptimisticOrder,
    45→    isOptimisticUpdate,
    46→    setIsOptimisticUpdate,
    47→  };
    48→}
    49→
```

```
interface ShotImageManagerDesktopProps extends ShotImageManagerProps {

  onClearPendingImageToOpen?: () => void;

  navigateWithTransition?: (doNavigation: () => void) => void;
}

export const ShotImageManagerDesktop: React.FC<ShotImageManagerDesktopProps> = ({
```

```
   139→    if (mobileSelectedIds.length === 0) {

   141→    }

   143→    try {
   144→      // Get the selected images and their current indices

   146→      const selectedItems = mobileSelectedIds.map(id => {
   147→        const image = currentImages.find(img => img.id === id);
   148→        const index = currentImages.findIndex(img => img.id === id);
   149→        return { id, image, currentIndex: index };

   151→
   152→      if (selectedItems.length === 0) {
   153→        return;
   154→      }

   156→      // Safety check: Ensure all images have id
   157→      const hasMissingIds = currentImages.some(img => !img.id);
   158→      if (hasMissingIds) {

   160→        return;

   162→
   163→      // Sort by current index to maintain relative order
   164→      selectedItems.sort((a, b) => a.currentIndex - b.currentIndex);
   165→
   166→      // Create new order by moving selected items to target position
   167→      const newOrder = [...currentImages];
   168→      
   169→      // Remove selected items from their current positions (in reverse order to maintain indices)
   170→      selectedItems.reverse().forEach(item => {
   171→        newOrder.splice(item.currentIndex, 1);
   172→      });
   173→      
   174→      // Insert selected items at target position (maintaining their relative order)
   175→      selectedItems.reverse().forEach((item, i) => {

   178→
   179→      // Create ordered IDs array for the unified system (safe now - checked above)
   180→      const orderedIds = newOrder.map(img => img.id);
   181→

   183→      const draggedItemId = selectedItems.length === 1 ? selectedItems[0].id : undefined;

   186→      setIsOptimisticUpdate(true);

   238→
   239→  // Check if item would actually move

   252→  }, [mobileSelectedIds, currentImages]);
   253→
```

## Area 1: LoraSelectorModal

**Original sizes:** `LoraSelectorModal.tsx` 276 lines, `useLoraFilters.ts` 225 lines.

**Q1 — Was original genuinely too large?**
`LoraSelectorModal.tsx` at 276 lines was borderline — not over the 300-line threshold. `useLoraFilters.ts` at 225 lines was under the threshold. Neither was clearly due for extraction on size grounds alone.

**Q2 — Are splits along real domain boundaries?**
`useLoraEditing.ts` (34 lines) extracts tab/editing state that was genuinely a coherent sub-concern. `LoraSelectorFooter.tsx` (137 lines) is a real visual section that lived at the bottom of the modal. Both splits are domain-meaningful.

The new `useLoraFilters.ts` (68 lines) is a different story. The old `useLoraFilters.ts` (225 lines) was the full filter/sort/pagination logic that computed `processedLoras`, `paginatedLoras`, etc. — genuinely a hook. The *new* `useLoraFilters.ts` is just UI state management (checkboxes, page, model filter) that previously lived in the parent component. It does not include the actual filtering computation. This hook name is now misleading — it no longer filters anything; it just stores the filter-state parameters that get passed down to `CommunityLorasTab`.

**Q3 — Trivially small files?**
`useLoraEditing.ts` at 34 lines is tiny — 8 lines of state, 3 trivial handlers. It's not meaningfully smaller than inlining it in the parent (the parent went from 276 to 160 lines, and 40 of those lines are the footer JSX that moved out). This extraction adds a file for state that amounts to two `useState` calls.

**Q4 — Passthrough wrappers?**
`LoraSelectorFooter` is not a passthrough — it genuinely owns its JSX. Clean.

**Q5 — Documentation/context lost?**
No significant comments in the original footer block. Fine.

**Q6 — Behavior changes?**
None detected. State shape and logic is identical.

**Q7 — Type-only files?**
Not applicable here.

**Summary:** Structurally reasonable. One naming problem: the new `useLoraFilters.ts` no longer filters anything — it stores filter *state* for the parent. Either rename it (`useLoraFilterState`) or (better) fold `useLoraEditing` back into it and rename to `useLoraSelectorState`. `useLoraEditing.ts` at 34 lines is below the threshold for extraction to be worth the added indirection.

---

## Area 2: OnboardingModal

**Original size:** 619 lines (a single file with all step components, helper functions, and the modal itself).

**Q1 — Was original genuinely too large?**
619 lines — yes, comfortably above the 300-line threshold.

**Q2 — Are splits along real domain boundaries?**
Yes. Six step components, a hook, a data module, a lib module, and types — all map to distinct concerns. The split is clean.

**Q3 — Trivially small files?**
`types.ts` is 17 lines with a single consumer (the modal file). It exports `OnboardingModalProps`, `OnboardingStepProps`, `OnboardingStepComponent`, and `OnboardingStepDefinition` — four types used across multiple step files. It's small but serves a real cross-file purpose.

`onboardingColors.ts` is 18 lines. The `getStepColors` function and its `OnboardingStepColors` interface are used in every step file. Reasonable.

`onboardingSteps.ts` is 16 lines — purely a data module that registers the step array. It's the kind of thing you'd want in its own file to add/remove steps without touching logic. Fine.

`IntroductionStep.tsx` at 43 lines and `CommunityStep.tsx` at 48 lines are very small. They were small in the original too (similar blocks of JSX). Acceptable given the 1-step-per-file principle, which matches how these were documented in the original.

**Q4 — Passthrough wrappers?**
None.

**Q5 — Documentation/context lost?**
The original had a comment on `GenerationMethodStep`: *"Lazy-loaded to improve modal performance"* and *"Only loads when this step is actually rendered, improving initial modal performance."* This comment is gone in the new `GenerationMethodStep.tsx`. The reasoning was meaningful: the original used a `switch/case` inside `renderCurrentStep()` to avoid mounting unused step components. **This is a behavior change.**

**Q6 — Behavior changes?**
Yes — a significant one. The original `renderCurrentStep()` was an explicit `switch/case`:

```ts
case 3:
  return <GenerationMethodStep onNext={handleNext} />;
```

This ensured only the current step's component was mounted. The new implementation uses:

```ts
const CurrentStepComponent = currentStepDefinition.component;
// ...
<CurrentStepComponent onNext={handleNext} onClose={onClose} />
```

This is functionally equivalent in terms of mounting (only one `CurrentStepComponent` renders per step). However, there is one subtle difference: the original `SetupCompleteStep` took `{ onClose }` as its only prop, while all other steps only took `{ onNext }`. In the new code, *all* step components use the `OnboardingStepProps` interface (`{ onNext, onClose }`), meaning every step now receives both `onNext` and `onClose`. For `IntroductionStep`, `CommunityStep`, `GenerationMethodStep`, `ThemeStep`, and `PrivacyDefaultsStep`, the `onClose` prop is simply unused — but passing it is harmless.

The more notable change is that `SetupCompleteStep` in the original was typed as `{ onClose: () => void }` (no `onNext`). In the new version it uses `OnboardingStepProps` which includes `onNext`. The component ignores `onNext`, so behavior is unchanged — but the type is looser than before.

The performance comment about lazy-loading is no longer accurate — both old and new use conditional rendering of only the active step, so performance is equivalent. The comment's removal just loses context, not behavior.

**Q7 — Type-only files?**
`types.ts` has 4 types used across 7+ files. Not single-consumer.

**Summary:** The split is well-justified (619 lines) and structurally good. One issue to flag: the removed comment about `GenerationMethodStep`'s lazy-load rationale should be preserved somewhere — its absence may mislead a future developer into thinking the data-driven `ONBOARDING_STEPS` array approach could be rendered all-at-once.

## Area 3: SettingsModal GenerationSection

**Original size:** 750 lines.

**Q1 — Was original genuinely too large?**
750 lines — well over the threshold. Extraction is justified.

**Q2 — Are splits along real domain boundaries?**
- `CommandPreview.tsx` (67 lines): the command code block with copy/reveal/hide controls. Clearly reusable.
- `GenerationTokenPanel.tsx` (38 lines): the "you need an API key" prompt. Distinct concern.
- `useCommandVisibility.ts` (43 lines): show/hide and scroll-into-view logic for command blocks.
- `useCopyFeedback.ts` (27 lines): 3 copied states + a shared timeout helper.
- `generationLabels.ts` (24 lines): 4 label maps.

All splits map to genuine sub-concerns.

**Q3 — Trivially small files?**
`GenerationTokenPanel.tsx` at 38 lines is borderline. The original had this as an inline conditional (~16 lines of JSX at line 243). Extracting 16 lines of JSX into a 38-line file adds a file, an interface, and an import — for a component that has a single caller and no behavior of its own. It guards on `hasValidToken` (which the parent already guards on before rendering), making the internal check redundant.

`generationLabels.ts` at 24 lines is 4 record constants. These were `const` declarations at the top of the original. Extracting them to their own file is unusual — they have one consumer (the GenerationSection itself). If `CommandPreview` ever needed labels, this would make sense, but `CommandPreview` doesn't need them. This is a constants file with a single consumer.

`useCopyFeedback.ts` at 27 lines is functionally equivalent to 12 lines inlined in the parent (3 state declarations + 3 `setTimeout` calls). The `triggerCopyFeedback` abstraction adds a layer but the hook is called in a way that creates 3 inline closures anyway (`markInstallCopied: () => triggerCopyFeedback(setCopiedInstallCommand)`). The abstraction is marginally useful but the hook could not be reused elsewhere without modification.

**Q4 — Passthrough wrappers?**
`GenerationTokenPanel` is not a passthrough — it owns its JSX. Fine.

**Q5 — Documentation/context lost?**
The original had detailed inline comments in the command-building functions that now moved to `commandUtils`. Those are in a separate file, not covered by this review, but nothing was lost from the parts being reviewed.

**Q6 — Behavior changes?**
One small change: the original `useCopyFeedback` had this inline for each copy handler:

```ts
setCopiedInstallCommand(true);
setTimeout(() => setCopiedInstallCommand(false), 3000);
```

The new `useCopyFeedback` wraps this in `triggerCopyFeedback`, called as `markInstallCopied: () => triggerCopyFeedback(setCopiedInstallCommand)`. Functionally identical.

`CommandPreview` is a clean extraction — behavior identical.

**Q7 — Type-only files?**
Not applicable.

**Summary:** Justified extraction given 750 lines. Two files are questionable: `generationLabels.ts` (4 constants, single consumer) could stay in the parent or move into `commandUtils.ts`; `GenerationTokenPanel.tsx` at 38 lines is too small for a standalone file with a single caller. These are minor issues.

## Area 4: ShotImageManager (Desktop + Mobile)

**Original sizes:** Desktop 390 lines, Mobile 440 lines.

**Q1 — Was original genuinely too large?**
Both files were above the 300-line threshold — extraction is justified.

**Q2 — Are splits along real domain boundaries?**
- `useImageTickFeedback.ts` (34 lines): 2 states + 2 auto-clear effects. Genuine extraction of a sub-concern.
- `useConfirmDialog.ts` (25 lines): open/pending state for the delete confirm dialog. Coherent.
- `useMobileImageSelection.ts` (69 lines): selection state, dispatch events, show-bar delay, tap handler. Clear domain.
- `useMobileOptimisticOrder.ts` (48 lines): optimistic reorder state with two sync effects. Clean.
- `mobileGridColumns.ts` (17 lines): a lookup map + one function.
- `DesktopImageGrid.tsx` (176 lines): the DnD-wrapped grid section. Genuine sub-component.
- `DesktopLightboxPanel.tsx` (61 lines): renders `DesktopLightboxOverlay`. **See Q4.**
- `DesktopSegmentViewer.tsx` (38 lines): renders `DesktopScrubbingPreview`. **See Q4.**

**Q3 — Trivially small files?**
`mobileGridColumns.ts` at 17 lines is just a map literal plus one function. This was previously an inline object in `ShotImageManagerMobile`. The map is only used in Mobile — single consumer. This is a utility extraction that doesn't justify a separate file; it would better live in `constants.ts` (which already exists in this directory).

`useConfirmDialog.ts` at 25 lines is small — two state values and three handlers. It was ~6 lines inline. This is just below the threshold where extraction adds clarity.

`useImageTickFeedback.ts` at 34 lines: the original Desktop component had an unnecessary `useCallback` wrapper around `setShowTickForSecondaryImageIdInternal` with a comment "Wrapper to log when setter is called." The extracted hook correctly eliminates this wrapper without the logging comment — a genuine cleanup.

**Q4 — Passthrough wrappers with identical props?**
`DesktopLightboxPanel.tsx` (61 lines): This is a pure passthrough. It accepts 14 props and passes all 14 directly to `DesktopLightboxOverlay` without modification, transformation, or conditional logic. The component adds no behavior, no defaulting, no rendering logic — it is a rename of `DesktopLightboxOverlay`. Every prop is forwarded 1-to-1. This is the definition of a passthrough wrapper and violates the "no passthrough wrappers" standard.

`DesktopSegmentViewer.tsx` (38 lines): Same problem. It accepts 7 props and passes all 7 directly to `DesktopScrubbingPreview` without modification. Pure passthrough, zero added value.

Both of these files exist to give the Desktop parent cleaner JSX, but the correct solution is to use `DesktopLightboxOverlay` and `DesktopScrubbingPreview` directly from the parent — which is what the original did.

**Q5 — Documentation/context lost?**
The original Desktop had meaningful comments explaining `capturedVariantIdRef`, `pendingImageToOpen`, and the `getGenerationId` usage. These are preserved in the new file. The original Mobile had a detailed comment explaining the optimistic state reset strategy and why it avoids flickering on shot navigation — this context is still present in `useMobileOptimisticOrder.ts`. No significant context lost.

**Q6 — Behavior changes?**
The original `handleMobileTap` in Mobile was:
```ts
const handleMobileTap = useCallback((imageId: string, _index: number) => { ... }, [mobileSelectedIds, readOnly]);
```

In the new `useMobileImageSelection.ts`:
```ts
const handleMobileTap = useCallback((imageId: string, _index?: number) => { ... }, [mobileSelectedIds, readOnly]);
```
`_index` changed from required to optional. This is a harmless loosening of the signature — no callers pass it, and it was `_index` (unused) in the original. No behavior change.

The original Mobile had cleanup of `dispatchAppEvent('mobileSelectionActive', false)` in the cleanup function of the selection effect. The new `useMobileImageSelection` preserves this exactly. Clean.

The original had `setMobileSelectedIds([])` in `performBatchDelete` and `handleJumpToShot` directly. In the new code these call `clearSelection()` from the hook, which calls `setMobileSelectedIds([])` and `onSelectionChange?.(false)`. The original's `handleJumpToShot` called `setMobileSelectedIds([])` directly without calling `onSelectionChange?.(false)`. The new `clearSelection()` now also fires `onSelectionChange?.(false)` from `handleJumpToShot`. This is a **subtle behavior change** — `onSelectionChange` is now called on jump-to-shot where it wasn't before. In practice this is probably the correct behavior (selection is cleared so the callback should fire), but it is a behavior change, not just a refactor.

**Q7 — Type-only files?**
Not applicable.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - **Component decomposition quality criteria**: Files should be >300 lines before splitting; splits must be along real domain boundaries; no passthrough wrappers (components that just forward all props to another component); no trivially small files (<30 lines) with single consumers
   - **Re-export shim anti-pattern**: Files that only `export { X } from './somewhere'` add indirection without value
   - **Hook-returning-JSX anti-pattern**: Hooks should return state/callbacks, not JSX elements via `useMemo`. Convert to `React.memo` components instead.
   - **Virtual-grouping barrels**: `index.ts` files that re-export hooks from `../` parent directory create misleading namespace groupings
   - **Dead code preservation tricks**: `void unusedVar;`, `_isVideo` underscore prefix on destructured-but-unused params
   - **Pick<> adapter types**: Narrow type aliases (e.g., `SharedVariantsInput = Pick<...>`) that exist only to bridge file boundaries from over-decomposition
   - React patterns: `React.memo`, `useMemo`, `useCallback`, `createContext`/`useContext`
